# Fil One Documentation

> Fil One is an S3-compatible object storage platform for teams that need
> reliable, cost-effective storage. Stored on the Filecoin network, where storage providers must
> continuously submit cryptographic proofs that they still hold the data they
> committed to store. No egress fees on paid plans, no per-request charges,
> $5.99/TB/month with a $5.99/month minimum.
> Standard S3 SDKs and tools work once you point them at your region's endpoint,
> `https://s3.<region>.filonecontent.com`, and enable path-style addressing, with
> standard Access Key ID / Secret Access Key auth. Some S3 features are missing
> (see S3 Compatibility). Endpoint, region and key must all refer to the same region.

Critical integration notes for developers:
- CreateBucket and DeleteBucket via the S3 API are region-dependent: supported
  in us-east-1, unavailable in eu-west-1 (use the dashboard there). The dashboard
  can delete a bucket in EVERY region, including eu-west-1, but only for Owner
  and Admin roles and only once the bucket is EMPTY (no objects or versions)
- Path-style addressing required: `https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com/bucket/key`
  (virtual-hosted-style URLs are not supported)
- Access keys are scoped to ONE region and cannot be used against another
- Region, versioning, Object Lock and retention are fixed at bucket creation and
  cannot be changed afterwards (no update-bucket operation). PutBucketVersioning,
  PutBucketObjectLockConfiguration and Get/PutBucketEncryption CANNOT BE GRANTED
  to any access key in either region; versioning and default retention are set
  only in the console's create form (under Advanced settings)
- Bucket names are unique within the region; names starting with `filone-rag-`
  are reserved
- Authentication: AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4). In boto3 set
  `Config(signature_version="s3v4")` explicitly so presigned URLs use SigV4
- AWS SDK for JavaScript v3.729+ adds CRC32 checksums by default; set
  `requestChecksumCalculation: "WHEN_REQUIRED"` and
  `responseChecksumValidation: "WHEN_REQUIRED"` on the S3Client, or presigned
  uploads fail with BadDigest
- Credentials: the console's Download .env uses the standard AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID /
  AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY names, which every SDK reads automatically
- All buckets are private by default; all data is encrypted at rest and in
  transit (TLS); encryption cannot be disabled. At-rest encryption is done by the
  regional storage gateway and keys are held by the regional operator, NOT by Fil
  One and NOT customer-managed. Do not name a specific cipher or SSE mode.
  SSE-KMS is rejected in BOTH regions (InvalidRequest in us-east-1; AccessDenied
  or InvalidRequest in eu-west-1). SSE-C is rejected in eu-west-1 and not yet
  confirmed in us-east-1 — send no encryption headers at all. No access key can
  be granted Get/PutBucketEncryption in either region
- Regions: eu-west-1 Europe (France, default) and us-east-1 US East (Michigan)
- Deletion is permanent and immediate on non-versioned buckets (no recycle bin).
  On versioned buckets an S3-API delete WITHOUT a version ID places a delete
  marker and prior versions are retained and still billed. The DASHBOARD NEVER
  WRITES A DELETE MARKER: a console delete (single or bulk) permanently removes
  the specific version on the row chosen, even on a versioned bucket
- CopyObject / server-side copy is confirmed working in us-east-1, including
  copying a specific version onto the current key to promote it (a version
  restore). In eu-west-1 PLAIN COPY WORKS but the version-id form is NOT YET
  CONFIRMED; download and re-upload is the fallback. The dashboard has no restore/roll-back button either way
- Per-object CIDs, deal IDs, and sealing state are NOT exposed — customers
  cannot independently audit an individual object
- A failed payment (past_due) makes the DASHBOARD READ-ONLY from the moment the
  payment fails, not after a later deadline; Stripe retries the charge. An
  organization OWNER can reactivate a canceled or disabled subscription from
  Billing -> Reactivate (no need to contact support)
- Trial caps are enforcement thresholds, not allowances: storage reaching 1 TB
  WRITE-LOCKS the account (lifted on the next usage run once storage is back
  under 1 TB); egress reaching 2 TB DISABLES it entirely, with NO read-only grace
  period first. Trial egress is a single cumulative budget over the 30 days.
  Enforced by a twice-daily job (~07:00/19:00 UTC), not in real time
- Storage is DECIMAL: 1 TB = 1,000 GB, 1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes
- Object Lock has NO grantable bypass permission: retention can be set or
  EXTENDED but NEVER SHORTENED, in either mode
- PutObjectRetention (per-object retention) and Legal Hold
  (Get/PutObjectLegalHold) work in BOTH REGIONS, including blocking delete while
  a hold is active. Both need the matching granular key
  permission, which is never granted automatically, and only an organization
  OWNER can create a key with PutObjectRetention or PutObjectLegalHold.
  Evidence differs by region: us-east-1 from the automated compatibility suite,
  eu-west-1 from engineering testing (the suite could not create a lock-enabled
  bucket there)
- The S3 API has NO IAM users, roles, or bucket policies: each request is allowed
  or refused by the access key's own permissions and bucket scope. The CONSOLE
  has organizations with four member roles (Owner, Admin, Member, Read only); a
  key can only carry permissions its creator's role holds
- Access keys can be ROTATED in the dashboard (new Access Key ID and secret,
  same name/permissions/buckets/region/expiry; old secret stops working at once)
- Object/part size limits (5 TB object, 5 GB single-PUT, 10,000 parts, 5 MB min
  part) are standard AWS S3 values, NOT independently confirmed for Fil One
- Bucket names forbid dots (unlike AWS S3); object keys are capped at 1,024
  CHARACTERS for dashboard uploads (code-backed); through the S3 API the standard
  S3 limit of 1,024 bytes applies but is NOT independently confirmed
- In eu-west-1, UNIMPLEMENTED OPERATIONS RETURN AccessDenied (403), NOT
  NotImplemented (501), and a bucket/key you cannot see returns 403 instead of
  404. A 403 from PutBucketPolicy, PutBucketAcl, PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration
  or the tagging operations means the FEATURE IS ABSENT, not that the key lacks
  a permission; PutBucketVersioning and PutBucketEncryption can't be granted to
  any key, so they fail the same way
- ACL requests fail two different ways in eu-west-1: a canned-ACL HEADER on an
  upload (--acl public-read) is SILENTLY IGNORED and the upload SUCCEEDS, while a
  DEDICATED call (Put/GetBucketAcl, Put/GetObjectAcl) is REJECTED with
  AccessDenied. Neither makes an object public
- Error CODES deviate from AWS in eu-west-1 even though the XML format is
  standard: BadDigest->InvalidArgument, InvalidRange->InvalidArgument,
  InvalidTag->BadRequest, BucketAlreadyExists->BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou. Some
  invalid requests are also ACCEPTED where AWS returns 400
- Open eu-west-1 client-affecting bugs: ListObjects NextMarker can carry an
  internal suffix (use ListObjectsV2 + ContinuationToken instead);
  EncodingType=url encodes a space as "+" not "%20"; additional-checksum
  operations are unreliable (ChecksumType may be missing from
  CompleteMultipartUpload responses)


---

# Welcome to Fil One

Source: https://docs.filone.com/

Fil One is an S3-compatible object storage platform designed for teams that need reliable, cost-effective storage, with Object Lock for write-once retention. If you've used AWS S3, you already know how to use Fil One.

## Get started

- [Quickstart](https://docs.filone.com/quickstart): Go from signup to your first upload.
- [S3 Compatibility](https://docs.filone.com/reference/s3-compatibility): See which S3 operations are supported and how to connect.
- [SDK Examples](https://docs.filone.com/sdk/overview): Copy-paste code examples for Python, JavaScript, Go, and CLI.

## Why Fil One

**S3-compatible from day one.** Use the tools you already know — AWS CLI, boto3, any S3-compatible SDK. Point your existing code at your region's endpoint, turn on path-style addressing, and it works. See [S3 Compatibility](https://docs.filone.com/reference/s3-compatibility) for the operations Fil One does not support.

**Backed by Filecoin.** Fil One stores your data on Filecoin, a distributed storage network where storage providers must continuously submit cryptographic proofs that they are still holding the data they committed to store, or face penalties.

**No egress fees on paid plans.** On a paid plan there are no data-transfer charges — download as much as you need. (The free trial has a 2 TB egress cap; see [Trial & Billing](https://docs.filone.com/billing/trial).)

**Simple, flat pricing.** Pay as you go at $5.99 / TB / month, with a $5.99 / month minimum. No per-request charges, no hidden fees, no tiered pricing. For volume pricing on 1, 3, or 5-year terms, talk to sales about the Business plan.

**30-day free trial.** 1 TB of storage and 2 TB of bandwidth, no credit card required.


---

# Quickstart

Source: https://docs.filone.com/quickstart

This guide walks you through creating an account, setting up credentials, and uploading your first object. Choose the path that fits your workflow.

## 1. Create your account

1. Go to [app.filone.com](https://app.filone.com) and sign up with your email, Google, or GitHub.
2. Verify your email address.
3. You're in. No credit card needed — your 30-day free trial starts automatically.

## 2. Create a bucket

From the dashboard, click **New bucket** to open the create form. Give the bucket a name (lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens; unlike AWS S3, Fil One does **not** allow dots) and pick a region:

| Setting | Options | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| Region | `eu-west-1` Europe (France) or `us-east-1` US East (Michigan) | Defaults to `eu-west-1`. Cannot be changed later. |
| Encryption | Always on | All data is encrypted at rest. Nothing to configure. |

Leave everything else at its default for your first bucket, and click **Create bucket**.

Warning: Some settings can only be chosen now
Versioning, Object Lock, and retention sit under **Advanced settings** on the create form, and can only be turned on when the bucket is created. Neither can be turned off later, and Object Lock can stop you deleting data you're paying for. Read [Versioning](https://docs.filone.com/storage/versioning) and [Object Lock](https://docs.filone.com/storage/object-lock) before you enable them on a bucket you plan to keep.

## 3. Upload your first object

Choose your preferred method. The App requires no API key. For CLI and SDK access, open your new bucket and click **Create API key**, or go to **API Keys** in the left menu and click **Create new key**. You'll get two values:

- **Access Key ID** — identifies the key (safe to store in config)
- **Secret Access Key** — authenticates your requests (treat like a password)

Note:
Your secret key is shown once. Copy it and store it securely. If you lose it, rotate the key from its **⋯** menu in **API Keys** to get a new secret. See [API Keys](https://docs.filone.com/app/api-keys#rotating-a-key).

A key also belongs to a single region, so create it in the same region as your bucket.

The examples below use `eu-west-1`, the default region. For a bucket in `us-east-1`, use `https://s3.us-east-1.filonecontent.com` and region `us-east-1` instead.

App:
1. Open your bucket from the dashboard.
2. Click **Upload object**, select one or more files (or drag a whole folder in), then click **Upload** to start the transfer.
3. Your objects appear in the file list once the upload completes.
4. To download: click the download icon on the object's row, or open the object's detail page and use the **Download** button in the header.

AWS CLI:
Create a `filone` profile so you don't overwrite your default AWS credentials. Requires [AWS CLI v2](https://docs.filone.com/sdk/cli). Enter your key's ID and secret when prompted, and leave the other prompts empty:

```bash
aws configure --profile filone
aws configure set region eu-west-1 --profile filone
aws configure set endpoint_url https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com --profile filone
# Path-style is required: Fil One does not support virtual-hosted URLs
aws configure set s3.addressing_style path --profile filone
```

Upload a file:

```bash
echo "hello" > my-file.txt
aws s3 cp my-file.txt s3://my-bucket/my-file.txt --profile filone
```

Verify it's there:

```bash
aws s3 ls s3://my-bucket/ --profile filone
```

Python (boto3):
Create `my-file.txt` first, for example with `echo "hello" > my-file.txt`.

```python
import boto3
from botocore.config import Config

s3 = boto3.client(
    "s3",
    endpoint_url="https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com",
    aws_access_key_id="YOUR_ACCESS_KEY",
    aws_secret_access_key="YOUR_SECRET_KEY",
    region_name="eu-west-1",
    config=Config(signature_version="s3v4", s3={"addressing_style": "path"}),
)

# Upload a file
s3.upload_file("my-file.txt", "my-bucket", "my-file.txt")

# List objects to confirm
response = s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket="my-bucket")
for obj in response.get("Contents", []):
    print(obj["Key"], obj["Size"])
```

JavaScript (AWS SDK v3):
Save this as `upload.mjs` (it uses ES modules and top-level `await`), then run `node upload.mjs`:

```javascript
import { S3Client, PutObjectCommand, ListObjectsV2Command } from "@aws-sdk/client-s3";
import { readFileSync } from "fs";

const client = new S3Client({
  endpoint: "https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com",
  region: "eu-west-1",
  forcePathStyle: true,
  // SDK v3.729+ adds checksums Fil One doesn't accept on presigned uploads
  requestChecksumCalculation: "WHEN_REQUIRED",
  responseChecksumValidation: "WHEN_REQUIRED",
  credentials: {
    accessKeyId: "YOUR_ACCESS_KEY",
    secretAccessKey: "YOUR_SECRET_KEY",
  },
});

// Upload a file
await client.send(new PutObjectCommand({
  Bucket: "my-bucket",
  Key: "my-file.txt",
  Body: readFileSync("my-file.txt"),
}));

// List objects to confirm
const { Contents } = await client.send(
  new ListObjectsV2Command({ Bucket: "my-bucket" })
);
Contents?.forEach((obj) => console.log(obj.Key, obj.Size));
```

## What's next

- [S3 Compatibility](https://docs.filone.com/reference/s3-compatibility): Full list of supported operations and headers.
- [SDK Examples](https://docs.filone.com/sdk/overview): Detailed examples for Python, JavaScript, Go, and CLI.
- [Billing & Trial](https://docs.filone.com/billing/trial): What's included in your trial and how to upgrade.

# Quickstart - AWS CLI

Source: https://docs.filone.com/quickstart/cli

Use the AWS CLI to upload, list and download objects in a Fil One bucket. You need a Fil One account and an API key. To create a key, open **API Keys** in the [console](https://app.filone.com), click **Create new key**, and pick the same region as your bucket. The secret is shown once.

## 1. Install the AWS CLI

Use **AWS CLI v2**, version 2.13 or later, so the CLI reads `endpoint_url` from your profile:

```bash
brew install awscli
# or follow the official installer:
# https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html
```

## 2. Configure credentials

Set up a named profile, so you don't overwrite your default AWS credentials and don't have to pass `--endpoint-url` on every command:

```ini
# ~/.aws/config
[profile filone]
endpoint_url = https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com
region = eu-west-1
s3 =
    addressing_style = path
```

The `addressing_style = path` line is required — Fil One only supports path-style URLs, and the CLI otherwise defaults to virtual-hosted style, which fails.

Note: The endpoint depends on your bucket's region
The example above uses `eu-west-1`, the default region. If your bucket is in `us-east-1`, use `https://s3.us-east-1.filonecontent.com` and `region = us-east-1` instead. The endpoint and the region must both match the bucket you are working with, and your access key has to belong to that region too.

If you use both regions, set up a profile per region (`[profile filone-eu]`, `[profile filone-us]`) and pick with `--profile`.

```ini
# ~/.aws/credentials
[filone]
aws_access_key_id = YOUR_ACCESS_KEY
aws_secret_access_key = YOUR_SECRET_KEY
```

## 3. Create a bucket

Whether `CreateBucket` works through the S3 API depends on the region. It is **not** available in `eu-west-1`, the default region. There, create the bucket in the [Fil One console](https://app.filone.com): click **New bucket**, enter `my-bucket` (or your own name), and click **Create bucket**.

In `us-east-1` you can create a bucket from the CLI, using a key that has the `CreateBucket` permission. This requires a `us-east-1` profile — define one the same way as the `filone` profile above but with the `us-east-1` endpoint and region (shown here as `filone-us`):

```bash
aws s3 mb s3://my-bucket --profile filone-us
```

Versioning and Object Lock can only be turned on when you create the bucket in the console. See [Buckets](https://docs.filone.com/storage/buckets).

The steps below use the `filone` profile (`eu-west-1`). If your bucket is in `us-east-1`, use `--profile filone-us` instead: the profile, the key and the bucket must all be in the same region.

## 4. Upload a file

```bash
echo "hello" > my-file.txt
aws s3 cp my-file.txt s3://my-bucket/ --profile filone
```

## 5. List objects

```bash
aws s3 ls s3://my-bucket/ --profile filone
```

## 6. Download the file

```bash
aws s3 cp s3://my-bucket/my-file.txt ./downloaded.txt --profile filone
```


---

# Quickstart - SDK

Source: https://docs.filone.com/quickstart/sdk

Choose your language and follow along. Each example uploads a file and verifies it. **Create the bucket first in the dashboard** — `CreateBucket` over the S3 API is not available in `eu-west-1`, the default region these examples use.

Note: The endpoint depends on your bucket's region
These examples use `eu-west-1`, the default region. For a bucket in `us-east-1`, use `https://s3.us-east-1.filonecontent.com` and region `us-east-1`. The endpoint, the region, and your access key must all refer to the same region.

Each example reads your key from the standard AWS environment variables, the same names the console's **Download .env** writes. Set them in your shell before you run an example, and keep the secret out of your code:

```bash
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=YOUR_ACCESS_KEY
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=YOUR_SECRET_KEY
```

The Python and JavaScript examples upload `my-file.txt`, so create it first: `echo "hello" > my-file.txt`.

Python:
```bash
pip install boto3
```

```python
import boto3
from botocore.config import Config

s3 = boto3.client(
    "s3",
    endpoint_url="https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com",
    region_name="eu-west-1",
    # Credentials come from AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    config=Config(signature_version="s3v4", s3={"addressing_style": "path"}),
)

# Upload a file (create the bucket first in the dashboard)
s3.upload_file("my-file.txt", "my-bucket", "my-file.txt")

# Verify
response = s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket="my-bucket")
for obj in response.get("Contents", []):
    print(f"{obj['Key']}  ({obj['Size']} bytes)")
```

JavaScript:
```bash
npm install @aws-sdk/client-s3
```

Save this as `upload.mjs` (it uses ES modules and top-level `await`), then run `node upload.mjs`:

```javascript
import { S3Client, PutObjectCommand, ListObjectsV2Command } from "@aws-sdk/client-s3";
import { readFileSync } from "fs";

const client = new S3Client({
  endpoint: "https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com",
  region: "eu-west-1",
  forcePathStyle: true,
  // SDK v3.729+ adds checksums Fil One doesn't accept on presigned uploads
  requestChecksumCalculation: "WHEN_REQUIRED",
  responseChecksumValidation: "WHEN_REQUIRED",
  // Credentials come from AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
});

// Upload a file (create the bucket first in the dashboard)
await client.send(new PutObjectCommand({
  Bucket: "my-bucket",
  Key: "my-file.txt",
  Body: readFileSync("my-file.txt"),
}));

// Verify
const { Contents } = await client.send(
  new ListObjectsV2Command({ Bucket: "my-bucket" })
);
Contents?.forEach((obj) => console.log(obj.Key, obj.Size));
```

Go:
```bash
mkdir filone-quickstart && cd filone-quickstart
go mod init example.com/filone-quickstart
go get github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/s3
go get github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/credentials
```

Save this as `main.go` and run `go run .`:

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "os"
    "strings"

    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/aws"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/credentials"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/s3"
)

func main() {
    client := s3.New(s3.Options{
        BaseEndpoint:  aws.String("https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com"),
        Region:        "eu-west-1",
        UsePathStyle:  true,
        Credentials: credentials.NewStaticCredentialsProvider(
            os.Getenv("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"),
            os.Getenv("AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"),
            "",
        ),
    })

    ctx := context.Background()

    // Upload (create the bucket first in the dashboard)
    _, err := client.PutObject(ctx, &s3.PutObjectInput{
        Bucket: aws.String("my-bucket"),
        Key:    aws.String("hello.txt"),
        Body:   strings.NewReader("Hello from Go!"),
    })
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    // List
    out, err := client.ListObjectsV2(ctx, &s3.ListObjectsV2Input{
        Bucket: aws.String("my-bucket"),
    })
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    for _, obj := range out.Contents {
        fmt.Printf("%s (%d bytes)\n", *obj.Key, *obj.Size)
    }
}
```

For more detailed examples including multipart uploads and presigned URLs, see the dedicated SDK pages:

- [Python](https://docs.filone.com/sdk/python): boto3: uploads, downloads, multipart, presigned URLs.
- [JavaScript](https://docs.filone.com/sdk/javascript): AWS SDK v3: the same operations from Node.js.
- [Go](https://docs.filone.com/sdk/go): aws-sdk-go-v2: the same operations from Go.


---

# Buckets

Source: https://docs.filone.com/storage/buckets

Buckets are containers for your objects. Every object in Fil One lives inside a bucket.

## Bucket naming rules

Bucket names must be:
- Between 3 and 63 characters
- Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only (**no dots**)
- Must start and end with a letter or number
- Unique within the region
- Not starting with `filone-rag-`, which is reserved

These rules are close to AWS S3's but not identical: in particular Fil One does **not** allow dots (`.`) in bucket names, which AWS S3 permits. If you are migrating a bucket whose name contains a dot, you will need to rename it.

## Creating a bucket

Note:
Whether you can create a bucket through the S3 API depends on the region. `CreateBucket` and `DeleteBucket` are supported in `us-east-1`, but not in `eu-west-1` — in that region buckets must be created in the Fil One console. All other S3 operations (uploading, downloading, listing objects, etc.) work normally via the API in every region.

To use `CreateBucket` or `DeleteBucket` with an access key, grant the key that permission when you create it. See [API Keys](https://docs.filone.com/security/api-keys).

1. From the dashboard, click **New bucket** to open the create form.
2. Enter a bucket name.
3. Choose a **region**: `eu-west-1` Europe (France, the default) or `us-east-1` US East (Michigan).
4. Optionally expand **Advanced settings** to turn on **Versioning**, then **Object Lock**, then **Retention**. Each needs the one before it: until it's on, the next switch shows a **Needs Versioning** or **Needs Object Lock** badge. Retention takes a mode (**Governance**, the default, or **Compliance**) and a duration from 1 day up to 100 years; it starts at 15 days. Leave Versioning off and the bucket keeps only the current copy of each object.
5. Click **Create bucket**. The console opens the new bucket's page, which offers **Create API key**. A key belongs to a single region and must match the bucket's region.

Every bucket is created with encryption enabled automatically.

Warning: Creation-time settings are permanent
Region, versioning, Object Lock, and retention cannot be changed after the bucket exists — there is no update-bucket operation, and a bucket cannot be moved between regions. To change any of them you have to create a new bucket and copy the data across. Enable versioning and Object Lock now if you are likely to want them.

## Listing buckets

AWS CLI:
```bash
aws s3 ls --endpoint-url https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com
```

Python (boto3):
```python
response = s3.list_buckets()
for bucket in response["Buckets"]:
    print(bucket["Name"], bucket["CreationDate"])
```

## Deleting a bucket

A bucket must be empty before it can be deleted, with no objects or object versions left in it.

App:
Open **Buckets**, choose **Delete bucket** from the bucket's actions menu, and confirm. If the bucket still holds objects, the dashboard tells you it is not empty. Open the bucket and use **Empty bucket** to remove everything first. See [Buckets in the console](https://docs.filone.com/app/buckets#deleting-a-bucket).

Dashboard deletion works in every region, including `eu-west-1`. Only the Owner and Admin roles can delete buckets.

AWS CLI:
```bash
aws s3 rb s3://my-bucket --endpoint-url https://s3.us-east-1.filonecontent.com --region us-east-1
```

`DeleteBucket` over the S3 API works in `us-east-1`, using a key that has the `DeleteBucket` permission. It is not available in `eu-west-1`, so use the dashboard there.

Info: Logical deletion and Filecoin storage
When you delete a bucket and its objects, the data is immediately removed from your Fil One account and is no longer accessible via the API or dashboard. Because Filecoin stores data in sealed sectors, the underlying storage may persist for a bounded period after deletion before it naturally expires. That residual data stays encrypted, and key custody sits with the regional storage operator rather than with you or Fil One — see [Encryption](https://docs.filone.com/security/encryption). The exact duration is set by the storage layer rather than measured by Fil One, and it does not affect your ability to manage your data in Fil One.


---

# Objects

Source: https://docs.filone.com/storage/objects

Objects are the files you store in Fil One. Each object consists of the file data, a key (the file path/name), and metadata.

## Uploading objects

App:
1. Open a bucket from the dashboard.
2. Click **Upload object**.
3. Select one or more files, or drag a whole folder in (an optional prefix lets you upload into a subpath), then click **Upload** to start the transfer.
4. Objects appear in the file list once the upload completes.

Folder uploads skip system files such as `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`, dot-files, and `__MACOSX` folders, and tell you how many were skipped. See [Uploading](https://docs.filone.com/app/buckets#uploading).

AWS CLI:
```bash
# Upload a single file
aws s3 cp my-file.txt s3://my-bucket/my-file.txt \
  --endpoint-url https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com

# Upload a directory
aws s3 sync ./local-folder s3://my-bucket/folder/ \
  --endpoint-url https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com
```

Python (boto3):
```python
# Upload a file
s3.upload_file("my-file.txt", "my-bucket", "my-file.txt")

# Upload with metadata (report.pdf must exist)
with open("report.pdf", "rb") as f:
    s3.put_object(
        Bucket="my-bucket",
        Key="report.pdf",
        Body=f,
        ContentType="application/pdf",
    )
```

For very large objects (above the single-PUT limit — see [Limits](https://docs.filone.com/limits)), use [multipart upload](https://docs.filone.com/storage/multipart-uploads).

## Downloading objects

App:
Click the download icon directly on the object's row in the file list, or click the file name to open its detail page and use the **Download** button in the header.

AWS CLI:
```bash
aws s3 cp s3://my-bucket/my-file.txt ./my-file.txt \
  --endpoint-url https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com
```

Python (boto3):
```python
s3.download_file("my-bucket", "my-file.txt", "my-file.txt")
```

## Listing objects

```bash
aws s3 ls s3://my-bucket/ --endpoint-url https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com
```

For programmatic listing with pagination:

```python
paginator = s3.get_paginator("list_objects_v2")
for page in paginator.paginate(Bucket="my-bucket"):
    for obj in page.get("Contents", []):
        print(obj["Key"], obj["Size"])
```

## Deleting objects

App:
Click the trash icon on an object's row, then confirm in the dialog. To delete several at once, tick their checkboxes and click **Delete** in the selection bar. To remove everything, including every earlier version, open the bucket and click **Empty bucket**. See [Deleting objects](https://docs.filone.com/app/buckets#deleting-objects).

The console deletes the specific version on the row you chose, so on a versioned bucket it removes that version permanently rather than writing a delete marker.

AWS CLI:
```bash
aws s3 rm s3://my-bucket/my-file.txt \
  --endpoint-url https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com
```

On a bucket without versioning, deletion is immediate — the object disappears from the dashboard and API instantly, and there is no recycle bin or soft-delete.

On a [versioned](https://docs.filone.com/storage/versioning) bucket, a delete over the S3 API without a version ID places a delete marker instead: the object stops appearing in listings, but prior versions are retained, remain downloadable by version ID, and continue to count as stored storage.

Info: Logical deletion and Filecoin storage
When you delete an object, it is immediately removed from your Fil One account and is no longer accessible. Because Filecoin stores data in sealed sectors, the underlying storage may persist for a bounded period after deletion before it naturally expires. That residual data stays encrypted, and key custody sits with the regional storage operator rather than with you or Fil One — see [Encryption](https://docs.filone.com/security/encryption). The exact duration is set by the storage layer rather than measured by Fil One, and it does not affect your ability to manage your data in Fil One.

## Presigned URLs

Generate a temporary URL that grants time-limited access to a specific object without requiring API credentials. The `s3` client is the one from [Python (boto3)](https://docs.filone.com/sdk/python#client-configuration), with `signature_version="s3v4"` set.

```python
# Generate a download URL valid for 1 hour
url = s3.generate_presigned_url(
    "get_object",
    Params={"Bucket": "my-bucket", "Key": "shared-report.pdf"},
    ExpiresIn=3600,
)
print(url)
```

Presigned URLs work for both `GetObject` (downloads) and `PutObject` (uploads). For uploads from the AWS SDK for JavaScript, see the [checksum setting](https://docs.filone.com/sdk/javascript#client-configuration) they need.

Warning: A presigned URL is a credential
Anyone who has the URL can use it until it expires, without signing in. Share it only with the people who should have access, and keep expiry times short. A **Share** link from the console lasts at most 7 days.


---

# Multipart Uploads

Source: https://docs.filone.com/storage/multipart-uploads

For very large objects you must use multipart upload. Under standard S3 behaviour the single-PUT ceiling is 5 GB — this is an AWS S3 limit that Fil One's storage gateway is expected to follow but that we have not independently confirmed (see [Limits](https://docs.filone.com/limits)). Multipart upload is also recommended for any file over 100 MB for improved reliability -- if a part fails, you retry only that part instead of the entire file.

Note:
The Fil One dashboard uploads objects with a single PUT, so multipart applies when you use your own S3 SDK or the AWS CLI, not the console upload flow.

## How it works

1. **Initiate** the upload and receive an upload ID.
2. **Upload parts** individually (minimum 5 MB each, except the last part).
3. **Complete** the upload by listing all parts. The service assembles the final object.

If something goes wrong, **abort** the upload to clean up incomplete parts.

## Example: AWS CLI

The AWS CLI handles multipart uploads automatically for large files:

```bash
# The AWS CLI switches to multipart above its own client-side threshold (8 MB by default)
aws s3 cp large-file.zip s3://my-bucket/large-file.zip \
  --endpoint-url https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com
```

To control thresholds:

```bash
aws configure set s3.multipart_threshold 100MB
aws configure set s3.multipart_chunksize 50MB
```

## Example: Python (boto3)

boto3 also handles multipart automatically via `upload_file`:

```python
from boto3.s3.transfer import TransferConfig

config = TransferConfig(
    multipart_threshold=100 * 1024 * 1024,  # 100 MB
    multipart_chunksize=50 * 1024 * 1024,   # 50 MB
    max_concurrency=10,
)

s3.upload_file(
    "large-file.zip",
    "my-bucket",
    "large-file.zip",
    Config=config,
)
```

## Limits

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Maximum object size | 5 TB |
| Maximum parts | 10,000 |
| Minimum part size | 5 MB (except last part) |
| Maximum part size | 5 GB |

Note:
These are the standard AWS S3 multipart limits. Fil One's storage gateway is expected to follow them, but we have not independently confirmed the exact values — treat them as guidance and test against your own workload before hard-coding a part size. See [Limits](https://docs.filone.com/limits).

## Cleaning up incomplete uploads

Incomplete multipart uploads are generally expected to consume storage until aborted. Fil One has **no lifecycle-rule mechanism** to expire them automatically (there is no `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` lifecycle support), so you must list and abort stale uploads yourself:

Note: Key permissions for cleanup
Listing in-progress uploads needs the **List** permission on your access key, and aborting one needs **Write**. Listing the parts of an upload goes with **Read**.

In `us-east-1`, access keys created before 26 August 2026 do not carry these multipart actions, so `list-multipart-uploads` and `abort-multipart-upload` fail with `403`. Existing keys cannot be updated: delete the key and create a new one to pick them up. See [API Keys](https://docs.filone.com/security/api-keys).

```bash
aws s3api list-multipart-uploads \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --endpoint-url https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com

aws s3api abort-multipart-upload \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key large-file.zip \
  --upload-id YOUR_UPLOAD_ID \
  --endpoint-url https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com
```


---

# Versioning

Source: https://docs.filone.com/storage/versioning

Versioning is **opt-in** and configured at bucket creation time. Once enabled on a bucket, it cannot be suspended or disabled. Every time you upload an object with the same key on a versioned bucket, Fil One creates a new version rather than overwriting the previous one.

Overwrites, and S3 API deletes without a version ID, keep every earlier version, so you can retrieve any previous state of an object by its version ID. Deleting a specific version, including any delete in the console, removes that version permanently.

To enable versioning, expand **Advanced settings** when you create a bucket in the console and turn on **Versioning**. Versioning is required for [Object Lock](https://docs.filone.com/storage/object-lock).

## How versions work

When you upload `reports/q1.pdf` for the first time, Fil One creates version `v1`. If you upload a new `reports/q1.pdf` tomorrow, Fil One creates version `v2` and `v1` remains intact. If you delete the object over the S3 API without a version ID, Fil One places a **delete marker** at the current version — the object appears deleted, but all previous versions are still retrievable.

This behavior applies to all objects in versioned buckets.

Warning: Deleting in the dashboard removes a version permanently
The dashboard never writes a delete marker. Deleting an object there, one at a time or in bulk, permanently deletes the specific version on the row you chose. Deleting the current version's row removes that version, and the earlier versions are left as they are. **Empty bucket** removes every version and delete marker in the bucket. See [Deleting objects](https://docs.filone.com/app/buckets#deleting-objects).

## Access key permissions for versions

Version-specific operations are separate granular permissions on an access key, and none of them is granted automatically. When you [create the key](https://docs.filone.com/security/api-keys), select the ones you need under the matching base permission:

| To do this | Grant | Under |
|------------|-------|-------|
| List object versions (`list-object-versions`) | **List object versions** (`ListBucketVersions`) | List |
| Download a specific version (`--version-id` on `get-object`) | **Read object versions** (`GetObjectVersion`) | Read |
| Delete a specific version or a delete marker | **Delete object versions** (`DeleteObjectVersion`) | Delete |

## Billing implications

Every version is a full copy of the object and is billed as stored storage. If you upload and then overwrite 100 files, you have 200 billable object versions consuming storage. Consider cleaning up old versions if storage cost is a concern. See [Pricing](https://docs.filone.com/billing/pricing).

## Listing versions

AWS CLI:
```bash
# List all versions in a bucket
aws s3api list-object-versions \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --profile filone

# List versions for a specific object
aws s3api list-object-versions \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --prefix reports/q1.pdf \
  --profile filone
```

Python (boto3):
```python
paginator = s3.get_paginator("list_object_versions")
for page in paginator.paginate(Bucket="my-bucket", Prefix="reports/q1.pdf"):
    for version in page.get("Versions", []):
        print(version["VersionId"], version["LastModified"], version["Size"])
    for marker in page.get("DeleteMarkers", []):
        print("DELETE MARKER", marker["VersionId"], marker["LastModified"])
```

## Retrieving a specific version

AWS CLI:
```bash
aws s3api get-object \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key reports/q1.pdf \
  --version-id YOUR_VERSION_ID \
  q1-old.pdf \
  --profile filone
```

Python (boto3):
```python
s3.download_file(
    "my-bucket",
    "reports/q1.pdf",
    "q1-old.pdf",
    ExtraArgs={"VersionId": "YOUR_VERSION_ID"},
)
```

## Going back to a previous version

The Fil One **dashboard** has no restore, roll-back, or "make current" button — you can list, download, and delete prior versions there, but not promote one to current.

Info: Region-dependent
Promoting a version to current with `CopyObject` is confirmed working in `us-east-1`. This has not yet been confirmed in `eu-west-1` — use the download-and-reupload method there instead.

### In `us-east-1`: copy the version onto the current key

Use `CopyObject` with `x-amz-copy-source-version-id` to promote an older version to current in place:

AWS CLI:
```bash
aws s3api copy-object \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key reports/q1.pdf \
  --copy-source "my-bucket/reports/q1.pdf?versionId=OLD_VERSION_ID" \
  --profile filone
```

Python (boto3):
```python
s3.copy_object(
    Bucket="my-bucket",
    Key="reports/q1.pdf",
    CopySource={
        "Bucket": "my-bucket",
        "Key": "reports/q1.pdf",
        "VersionId": "OLD_VERSION_ID",
    },
)
```

This creates a new current version with the old content; the version you copied from stays intact.

### In `eu-west-1`, or as a universal fallback: download and re-upload

To go back to an earlier version without `CopyObject`, download it and upload it again. The re-upload becomes a new current version, and the version you copied from stays intact.

AWS CLI:
```bash
aws s3api get-object \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key reports/q1.pdf \
  --version-id OLD_VERSION_ID \
  q1-restored.pdf \
  --profile filone

aws s3api put-object \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key reports/q1.pdf \
  --body q1-restored.pdf \
  --profile filone
```

Python (boto3):
```python
old = s3.get_object(
    Bucket="my-bucket",
    Key="reports/q1.pdf",
    VersionId="OLD_VERSION_ID",
)

s3.put_object(
    Bucket="my-bucket",
    Key="reports/q1.pdf",
    Body=old["Body"].read(),
)
```

If the current version is a delete marker, you can instead make the object visible again by deleting that delete marker by its version ID — see below.

## Delete markers

When you delete an object without specifying a version ID, Fil One places a **delete marker** at the top of the version stack. The object appears deleted in standard listings and `GetObject` returns `NoSuchKey`. The previous versions remain intact and can be retrieved by version ID.

To permanently delete a specific version (including a delete marker), specify the version ID in the delete request:

AWS CLI:
```bash
# Delete a specific version permanently
aws s3api delete-object \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key reports/q1.pdf \
  --version-id YOUR_VERSION_ID \
  --profile filone

# Remove a delete marker (restores the object to visible)
aws s3api delete-object \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key reports/q1.pdf \
  --version-id DELETE_MARKER_VERSION_ID \
  --profile filone
```

Python (boto3):
```python
# Delete a specific version permanently
s3.delete_object(
    Bucket="my-bucket",
    Key="reports/q1.pdf",
    VersionId="YOUR_VERSION_ID",
)
```

Warning:
Permanently deleting a version cannot be undone. If the version has an active Object Lock Compliance retention, the delete request will be rejected.

## Versioning and Object Lock

Object Lock is configured on the **bucket**, when the bucket is created. You enable it there and set a default retention mode and duration, and Object Lock requires versioning to be enabled on the same bucket. Neither can be turned on later.

Retention is then tracked per **version**. The bucket's default retention is applied to each new object version as it is uploaded, and each version carries its own retention independently — locking one version does not affect the versions above or below it, and older versions keep their own settings.

What that means in practice:

- You cannot delete a version that is under active Compliance retention, regardless of whether a delete marker exists above it.
- A delete marker is not itself protected by retention, so an object can still appear deleted while its underlying versions remain locked and intact.
- Because retention comes from the bucket default, a bucket with a long default retention will accumulate locked versions on every overwrite. Each one is billed as stored storage and cannot be removed until its retention expires.

See [Object Lock](https://docs.filone.com/storage/object-lock) for modes, durations, and examples.


---

# Object Lock

Source: https://docs.filone.com/storage/object-lock

Object Lock lets you enforce Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) protection on stored objects. Depending on the mode you choose, a locked object cannot be deleted or overwritten until its retention period expires — in **Compliance** mode, not even by the organization Owner. This is designed for data-retention, legal-preservation, and ransomware-protection use cases. Whether it satisfies a specific regulation is for your own compliance review to decide — see [On regulatory compliance](#on-regulatory-compliance) at the end of this page.

## Key concepts

**Retention period** — A duration during which an object version cannot be deleted or overwritten.

**Compliance mode** — The strictest protection. No user, including the organization Owner, can shorten the retention period or delete a locked object before it expires.

**Governance mode** — A softer protection. In standard S3, a caller holding a special *bypass* permission can override Governance retention and delete objects early. **Fil One does not currently expose a grantable bypass permission**, so in practice a Governance-locked object is protected for its retention period the same way a Compliance one is; the difference is that Governance is not positioned as an absolute, unbypassable guarantee at the platform level.

**Versioning** — Object Lock requires versioning, so you enable both when creating the bucket. Versioning cannot be suspended on any Fil One bucket once it is set.

## Enabling Object Lock

Object Lock is **opt-in** and must be enabled at **bucket creation time**. It cannot be added to an existing bucket, and once enabled it cannot be disabled.

To create a bucket with Object Lock:

1. From the dashboard, click **New bucket** to open the create form.
2. Enter a bucket name and choose a region.
3. Expand **Advanced settings** and turn on **Versioning**. Until you do, Object Lock shows a **Needs Versioning** badge.
4. Turn on **Object Lock**.
5. Turn on **Retention** and select a mode: **Governance** (the default) or **Compliance**.
6. Set a default retention duration, from 1 day up to 100 years (36,500 days). It starts at 15 days.
7. Click **Create bucket**.

Warning:
Object Lock must be enabled at bucket creation. It cannot be added to an existing bucket.

## Retention modes

| Mode | Can it be overridden early? | Typical use |
|------|-----------------------------|-------------|
| **Governance** (default) | Not through any Fil One-granted permission today | Internal-policy retention, audit-friendly workflows |
| **Compliance** | No — not by anyone, including organization Owners | Strict, long-term immutable record-keeping |

In **Compliance mode**, the retention period is absolute. No action can shorten or remove it once set.

In **Governance mode**, standard S3 allows a caller with the bypass permission to delete locked objects early. Fil One does not currently expose that permission, so today a Governance lock behaves like a firm retention lock rather than a routinely-overridable one. Choose it when you want WORM-style protection without positioning it as an absolute regulatory guarantee.

Warning:
Choose your retention mode carefully **at bucket creation** — it is fixed for the life of the bucket and cannot be changed afterwards. There is no update-bucket operation, so you cannot convert a Governance bucket into a Compliance one later. Moving objects into a bucket with a different mode means copying them into it with `CopyObject` over the S3 API (see [S3 Compatibility](https://docs.filone.com/reference/s3-compatibility)) or downloading and re-uploading them. Compliance retention periods, once set, cannot be shortened or removed.

## Setting per-object retention

The default retention period set at bucket creation is applied automatically to every object uploaded to that bucket.

Info: `PutObjectRetention` needs a granted permission
Setting or extending retention on an *individual* object version via `PutObjectRetention` works in **both regions**, but only with the **Set retention** permission, which is never granted automatically and only an organization Owner can grant. Retention can be extended but not shortened: no Fil One access key can be granted the bypass-governance permission. See [Key concepts](#key-concepts).

Object Lock buckets are always versioned, so a retention call should target a specific version with `--version-id`; without it the call targets whatever the current version is (possibly a delete marker).

The examples use Governance mode. Replace `YYYY-MM-DD` with a date a day or two from now while you're testing: you can extend retention later, but on Fil One you can't shorten it in either mode, because no key can be granted the bypass permission.

Danger: Compliance retention can't be shortened or removed
If you set `"Mode": "COMPLIANCE"`, nobody, including the organization Owner, can delete that version or shorten its retention until the date passes. The data keeps being billed until then, up to 100 years.

AWS CLI:
```bash
aws s3api put-object-retention \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key important-record.pdf \
  --version-id YOUR_VERSION_ID \
  --retention '{"Mode": "GOVERNANCE", "RetainUntilDate": "YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z"}' \
  --endpoint-url https://s3.us-east-1.filonecontent.com \
  --region us-east-1
```
Python (boto3):
```python
s3.put_object_retention(
    Bucket="my-bucket",
    Key="important-record.pdf",
    VersionId="YOUR_VERSION_ID",
    Retention={
        "Mode": "GOVERNANCE",
        "RetainUntilDate": "YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z",
    },
)
```

In standard S3, retention can be extended but never shortened: you can move `RetainUntilDate` further into the future but not closer, and shortening a Compliance retention period is rejected (with `403 AccessDenied`). Fil One's `us-east-1` gateway has been confirmed to follow this; `eu-west-1` has not yet been independently verified.

## Checking retention status

The object detail page in the dashboard shows an object's retention status, and displays a lock banner for Compliance-locked objects — so you don't need the CLI just to check. `GetObjectRetention` is also available over the S3 API:

```bash
aws s3api get-object-retention \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key important-record.pdf \
  --version-id YOUR_VERSION_ID \
  --endpoint-url https://s3.us-east-1.filonecontent.com \
  --region us-east-1
```

Returns:

```json
{
  "Retention": {
    "Mode": "GOVERNANCE",
    "RetainUntilDate": "YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00+00:00"
  }
}
```

## Deleting locked objects

Attempting to delete an object with active retention returns `403 AccessDenied`.

On a versioned bucket, a `DELETE` request without a version ID places a delete marker. The object appears deleted to applications, but the underlying version remains protected and intact until retention expires.

## Deleting buckets with locked objects

A bucket can only be deleted once it is empty, and objects under active retention cannot be deleted, so a bucket holding locked versions cannot be removed until their retention expires and you delete them. **Empty bucket** in the dashboard reports locked objects as ones it could not delete and leaves them in place.

Once the bucket is empty, delete it from the dashboard in either region (Owner and Admin roles only), or over the S3 API with `DeleteBucket` in `us-east-1`. `DeleteBucket` is not available over the S3 API in `eu-west-1`. See [Buckets](https://docs.filone.com/storage/buckets#deleting-a-bucket).

## Object Lock and API keys

`GetBucketVersioning` and `GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration` are pre-selected when you create a key. Untick them if the key shouldn't read a bucket's versioning or Object Lock settings. Beyond that:

- A key with **Delete** permission can delete objects in **Governance** mode buckets once retention has expired. Fil One does not expose a bypass permission for deleting *before* expiry.
- **Compliance** mode cannot be overridden by any key, regardless of permissions.
- To set retention on an individual version, grant the **Set retention** permission (Owner-only to grant). See the [note above](#setting-per-object-retention). It is available in both regions and is never granted automatically.

## Object Lock during trial

Object Lock is fully available during the free trial, with no trial-specific retention cap. Trial and paid accounts alike can set retention periods from **1 day to 100 years** (36,500 days).

Warning: A trial lock cannot be undone
Retention outlives the trial: a lock you set during the trial still applies after it ends, and Compliance retention cannot be shortened once set. Because durations run up to 100 years, an object you Compliance-lock while testing keeps occupying storage — and generating storage cost once you are on a paid plan — for the entire retention period, with no way to delete it early. Use short durations while evaluating.

## Object Lock and the Filecoin storage model

When you delete an object after its retention period expires, it is immediately removed from your Fil One account and inaccessible via the API and dashboard. Because Filecoin stores data in sealed sectors, the underlying storage may persist for a bounded period until the sector naturally expires; the exact duration is set by the storage layer rather than measured by Fil One. That residual data stays encrypted, and key custody sits with the regional storage operator rather than with you or Fil One — see [Encryption](https://docs.filone.com/security/encryption). Whether that bounded persistence matters for a particular regulatory obligation is a question for your own compliance review — this documentation does not make that determination.

## Common use cases

Object Lock provides WORM-style retention. These are common scenarios where teams reach for that capability — they describe the use case, not a claim that Fil One is certified for the named regulation (see the note below):

| Use case | Typical retention | What Object Lock provides |
|----------|-------------------|---------------------------|
| Financial records | 6–7 years | Immutable, non-rewritable storage for the retention period |
| Healthcare records | 6–10 years | Prevents deletion or overwrite of records under retention |
| Ransomware-resistant backup | 30–90 days | Backups cannot be encrypted-over or deleted while locked |
| Legal preservation | Variable | Retention-based preservation of evidence, or S3 *Legal Hold* |
| Audit-log retention | Varies | Keeps logs unmodified for a fixed window |

## On regulatory compliance

Object Lock provides WORM-style retention, which is a building block many regulatory regimes call for. However:

- Fil One holds **no third-party compliance attestation** (for example, an SEC 17a-4 assessment) for this feature.
- Retention enforcement at the storage gateway is confirmed in both regions, but by different means: `us-east-1` by an automated compatibility suite, `eu-west-1` by engineering testing rather than that suite. If a specific obligation depends on it, validate the exact behaviour you need.
- The product surfaces **no per-object cryptographic proof** (no CID, deal ID, or seal state) that you could present to an auditor to demonstrate integrity.

Treat the regulations named above as illustrative use cases, and evaluate whether Object Lock meets a specific obligation as part of your own compliance process.


---

# Account Security

Source: https://docs.filone.com/security/account-security

This page covers securing the account you sign in with. For authenticating **API requests**, which is a separate mechanism, see [Authentication](https://docs.filone.com/security/authentication) and [API Keys](https://docs.filone.com/security/api-keys).

## Signing in

Fil One supports four sign-in methods:

- **Passkeys**, the primary method
- **Google**
- **GitHub**
- **Email with password**

A new account must verify its email address before the dashboard opens. Until you do, every page redirects to a verification screen.

## Two-factor authentication

Two-factor authentication is opt-in per user and managed from **Settings**, under **Security**. Three factor types are supported:

| Factor | Shown in the dashboard as | What it is |
|--------|---------------------------|------------|
| Authenticator app | **Authenticator app (OTP)** | A time-based one-time code from an app such as 1Password, Authy, or Google Authenticator |
| Security key | **Security key** | A roaming WebAuthn authenticator, for example a YubiKey |
| Device biometrics | **Device biometrics** | A platform WebAuthn authenticator: Face ID, Touch ID, or Windows Hello |

**SMS and email codes are deliberately not offered.** Both are vulnerable to SIM-swap and mailbox-compromise attacks, so Fil One only supports factors bound to a device or an app.

You can enrol more than one factor and remove individual ones from Settings.

Signing in with a passkey counts as a strong factor, so you aren't asked for a second factor on top of it.

## Passkeys

Passkeys are listed separately from two-factor methods in Settings, under **Passkeys**. If you have none enrolled, the dashboard prompts you to add one on your next sign-in.

You can hold up to **20 passkeys** on one account, which is enough to cover several devices without having to retire an old one to add a new one.

Accounts that sign in with Google or GitHub don't see the **Passkeys** section.

## Recovery codes

A recovery code is a single-use code for signing in if you lose access to your authenticator. Generate or replace one from **Settings** → **Security** → **Recovery code** → **Regenerate**.

Generating a new code invalidates the previous one, so store the new value somewhere durable before you close the dialog.

Signing in with a recovery code assumes you've lost your device, so the same sign-in asks you to set up a new two-factor method before you reach the console. Have an authenticator app or a passkey ready.

## Changes to security settings require re-authentication

Four actions require a session that was signed in with two-factor authentication or a passkey, even inside an already signed-in session:

- Removing a two-factor method
- Removing all two-factor methods
- Removing a passkey
- Regenerating a recovery code

If your current session wasn't, the dashboard sends you back through sign-in to step up before the action proceeds. This means a session signed in with a password alone cannot strip the account's protections.

Transferring ownership of an organization has a stricter check: you must have signed in within the last five minutes, and if you have two-factor authentication set up, that sign-in must include it or use a passkey. Otherwise the dashboard sends you back through sign-in first.

## Changing your password

Change your account password from **Settings** → **Security** → **Password** → **Change**. This sends a password-reset email to your registered address.

If you sign in with Google or GitHub, there is no password to change in Fil One. **Settings** shows the password as **Managed by Google** (or **GitHub**), with a link to update it with that provider.

## Related

- [Authentication](https://docs.filone.com/security/authentication): signing API requests with SigV4
- [API Keys](https://docs.filone.com/security/api-keys): creating and scoping keys for programmatic access


---

# Authentication

Source: https://docs.filone.com/security/authentication

All API requests to Fil One must be authenticated using AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4). This is the same authentication method used by AWS S3, so any S3-compatible SDK or tool handles it automatically.

Note: Looking for account sign-in?
This page is about signing **API requests**. For the account you log into the dashboard with, including two-factor authentication, passkeys, and recovery codes, see [Account Security](https://docs.filone.com/security/account-security).

Note: Keys and endpoints are region-specific
Every access key belongs to a **single region**, chosen when you create it, and it only authenticates requests to that region's endpoint. Examples below use `eu-west-1`, the default region — for `us-east-1`, use `https://s3.us-east-1.filonecontent.com` and region `us-east-1`. If you store data in both regions you need a key for each.

## API keys

Each API key consists of two parts:

| Component | Description | Example format |
|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| **Access Key ID** | Identifies the key. Included in request headers. | `FHXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX` |
| **Secret Access Key** | Signs your requests. Never sent over the wire. | `EXAMPLEfakeSECRETkeyDoNotUse...` |

Your secret key is displayed **once** at creation time. Store it securely. If you lose it, [rotate the key](https://docs.filone.com/security/api-keys#rotating-a-key) to get a new key pair.

## Creating an API key

Create keys in the console under **API Keys** → **Create new key**. Pick the **Region** carefully: a key only authenticates against its own region's endpoint, and a key created in the wrong region fails with `403`, the most common first-run mistake. See [Creating an API key](https://docs.filone.com/security/api-keys#creating-an-api-key) for the steps and what each permission allows.

You can create multiple API keys per account. A key can only carry permissions your role in the organization holds, and Read only members cannot create keys. See [API Keys](https://docs.filone.com/security/api-keys) for details on configuring key permissions.

## Revoking an API key

Go to **API Keys** in the left menu, find the key, open its **⋯** action menu, and choose **Delete**. Deletion is forwarded to the regional storage operator; the key stops working once that change propagates, so rotate any dependent credentials rather than assuming an exact cut-off instant.

## Configuring your client

### AWS CLI

Use **AWS CLI v2**, version 2.13 or later, which reads `endpoint_url` from the profile. Configure credentials into a named `filone` profile (not the default), so they land where `--profile filone` will read them:

```bash
aws configure --profile filone
```

When prompted, enter your Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, and `eu-west-1` as the region. Then add the endpoint and path-style setting to the same profile:

```ini
# ~/.aws/config
[profile filone]
endpoint_url = https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com
region = eu-west-1
s3 =
    addressing_style = path
```

Then use `--profile filone` on your commands. Path-style addressing is required — without it the CLI uses virtual-hosted URLs that fail against Fil One.

### Python (boto3)

Load credentials from the `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` environment variables (recommended), which boto3 reads automatically. They're also the names the console's **Download .env** writes. Set `region_name` (SigV4 needs a signing region), path-style addressing, and SigV4 for presigned URLs:

```python
import boto3
from botocore.config import Config

s3 = boto3.client(
    "s3",
    endpoint_url="https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com",
    region_name="eu-west-1",
    config=Config(signature_version="s3v4", s3={"addressing_style": "path"}),
)
```

For a quick local test only, you can pass credentials inline — never commit this to source control:

```python
import boto3
from botocore.config import Config

s3 = boto3.client(
    "s3",
    endpoint_url="https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com",
    aws_access_key_id="YOUR_ACCESS_KEY",
    aws_secret_access_key="YOUR_SECRET_KEY",
    region_name="eu-west-1",
    config=Config(signature_version="s3v4", s3={"addressing_style": "path"}),
)
```

### JavaScript (AWS SDK v3)

```javascript
import { S3Client } from "@aws-sdk/client-s3";

const client = new S3Client({
  endpoint: "https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com",
  region: "eu-west-1",
  forcePathStyle: true,
  // SDK v3.729+ adds checksums Fil One doesn't accept on presigned uploads
  requestChecksumCalculation: "WHEN_REQUIRED",
  responseChecksumValidation: "WHEN_REQUIRED",
  // Credentials come from AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
});
```

### Go

```go
package main

import (
    "os"

    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/aws"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/credentials"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/s3"
)

func newClient() *s3.Client {
    return s3.New(s3.Options{
        BaseEndpoint: aws.String("https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com"),
        Region:       "eu-west-1",
        UsePathStyle: true,
        Credentials: credentials.NewStaticCredentialsProvider(
            os.Getenv("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"),
            os.Getenv("AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"),
            "",
        ),
    })
}
```

## Security best practices

- **Do not hardcode credentials** in source code. Use environment variables, a secrets manager, or credential files.
- **Create separate keys** for different environments (development, staging, production).
- **Rotate keys periodically.** Use **Rotate** in the key's **⋯** menu, then deploy the new credentials. The old secret stops working as soon as the new one is issued. See [Rotating a key](https://docs.filone.com/security/api-keys#rotating-a-key).
- **Revoke keys immediately** if you suspect they have been compromised.


---

# API Keys

Source: https://docs.filone.com/security/api-keys

API keys authenticate your requests to the Fil One S3 API. Each key consists of an **Access Key ID** (public identifier) and a **Secret Access Key** (used to sign requests).

## Creating an API key

1. Go to **API Keys** in the left sidebar of the console.
2. Click **Create new key** (this opens a dedicated page).
3. Give the key a descriptive name (e.g., `production-backend`, `ci-pipeline`). Names are limited to 64 characters (letters, numbers, spaces, and `_ - .`), and names starting with `filone-console` (in any capitalization) are reserved.
4. Choose the key's **region** (see [Region scope](#region-scope)). It is pre-set to `eu-west-1`, and it is fixed for the life of the key.
5. Set the key's permissions and bucket scope (see below). **Read**, **Write**, and **List** are pre-selected, along with the two bucket configuration reads. For a read-only key, untick **Write**. At least one permission is required, and you can only grant permissions your role holds (see [Who can create and manage keys](#who-can-create-and-manage-keys)).
6. Optionally set an expiration: **Never expires**, **30 days**, or a **Custom** date.
7. Click **Create API key**.
8. **Copy the Secret Access Key immediately.** It is shown only once. If you lose it, [rotate the key](#rotating-a-key) to get a new one. If you use **Download .env** or **Download .csv**, the file holds the secret in plain text: move it into your secrets store or credential file, delete the download, and never commit it.

## Key permissions

### Object permissions

Each key can be granted a combination of the following object-level permissions:

| Permission | What it allows |
|------------|----------------|
| **Read** | `GetObject` (and `HeadObject`, which uses the same underlying permission), `ListMultipartUploadParts`. In `us-east-1`, also `ListBucket` |
| **Write** | `PutObject`, `AbortMultipartUpload` |
| **List** | `ListObjectsV2` / `ListBucket`, and listing in-progress multipart uploads (`ListBucketMultipartUploads`) |
| **Delete** | `DeleteObject` |

You can grant any combination of these permissions. A key with only **Read** and **List** permissions is suitable for read-only access, such as a CDN or analytics pipeline. A key with **Write** but not **Delete** can upload new objects and overwrite existing ones, but cannot delete them. Overwriting replaces an object's data, so on a bucket without [versioning](https://docs.filone.com/storage/versioning) a **Write** key can still destroy data. Use versioning or [Object Lock](https://docs.filone.com/storage/object-lock) if that matters.

The **Read** grant differs by region. In `us-east-1` it also includes `ListBucket`, so a key with **Read** but not **List** can still list object names there. In `eu-west-1`, **Read** does not include listing.

Listing the *names* of your buckets (`ListAllMyBuckets`) is granted to every key automatically and is not one of the permissions above. Multipart uploads (`CreateMultipartUpload`, `UploadPart`, `CompleteMultipartUpload`) need **Write**. See [Multipart Uploads](https://docs.filone.com/storage/multipart-uploads).

### Bucket management permissions

These are standalone permissions — they do not require any object permission. They can only be granted in regions where bucket management is available through the S3 API. In `eu-west-1` they appear on the create form but are disabled, with the tooltip **Not supported in Europe (France)**, so they cannot be granted on an `eu-west-1` key. See [Buckets](https://docs.filone.com/storage/buckets).

| Permission | What it allows |
|------------|----------------|
| `CreateBucket` | Create a new bucket |
| `DeleteBucket` | Delete an empty bucket |

Listing buckets is always permitted and is not a separate, configurable permission.

### Bucket configuration permissions

These read a bucket's settings and are selectable in every region, including `eu-west-1`. The create form in the console pre-selects both, so untick them if your key doesn't need them.

| Permission | What it allows |
|------------|----------------|
| `GetBucketVersioning` | Read whether versioning is enabled on a bucket |
| `GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration` | Read a bucket's default Object Lock retention policy |

### Granular permissions

You can enable additional granular permissions on top of the basic object permissions. Each granular permission requires only its **parent basic permission** — the bucket does **not** need versioning or Object Lock enabled for the permission to be selectable:

| Granular permission | Requires basic | What it allows |
|---------------------|----------------|----------------|
| `GetObjectVersion` | Read | Retrieve specific versions of an object |
| `GetObjectRetention` | Read | View retention policy on an object |
| `GetObjectLegalHold` | Read | View legal hold status on an object |
| `PutObjectRetention` | Write | Apply or modify retention policies |
| `PutObjectLegalHold` | Write | Apply or remove legal holds |
| `ListBucketVersions` | List | List all versions of objects in a bucket |
| `DeleteObjectVersion` | Delete | Permanently delete a specific object version |

Granular permissions are additive — a key must have the corresponding basic permission before a granular permission can be granted. For example, `PutObjectRetention` requires the **Write** basic permission.

`PutObjectRetention` and `PutObjectLegalHold` (**Set retention** and **Set legal hold** in the console) can only be granted by an Owner. For other roles, the create form doesn't show them.

Note:
Granting `PutObjectRetention` makes the permission available on the key. Per-object retention calls work in both regions. See [S3 Compatibility](https://docs.filone.com/reference/s3-compatibility#object-lock).

Note:
`GetObjectLegalHold` and `PutObjectLegalHold` can be granted on a key. Legal Hold operations work through the S3 API in both regions. See [S3 Compatibility](https://docs.filone.com/reference/s3-compatibility#object-lock).

## Who can create and manage keys

A key can only carry permissions that your [role](https://docs.filone.com/app/organization#roles-and-permissions) in the organization holds, and the create form only offers those. What each role can do with keys:

- **Read only** members cannot create keys and don't see the key list.
- **Members** can create keys, and see, rotate, and delete only the keys they created.
- **Admins** and **Owners** can create keys and see, rotate, and delete every key in the organization.

Keys follow the person who created them.

Warning: Membership changes revoke keys
If a member's role is narrowed, any key they created that the new role couldn't create is revoked. Removing a member from the organization revokes every key they created, and so does transferring ownership for keys an Admin can't hold. The revoked keys stop working immediately, and the member is emailed a list of them. Before you change someone's access, move any application that uses their keys onto a new key.

## Region scope

Every key belongs to a **single region**, chosen when you create it. A key only authenticates requests to that region's endpoint — it cannot be used against another region, and it cannot be moved to one afterward. If you store data in both `eu-west-1` and `us-east-1`, you need a separate key for each.

The region also determines which permissions are available: the bucket management permissions above cannot be granted on an `eu-west-1` key.

## Bucket scope

By default, a key has access to all buckets in the key's region. You can restrict a key to one or more specific buckets, which limits **object operations** to that set. Note that listing your bucket *names* (`ListAllMyBuckets`) is always permitted, so bucket scoping restricts access to bucket **contents** rather than hiding that other buckets exist.

This is useful when:
- Different services need access to different buckets
- You want to limit the blast radius of a compromised key
- External vendors or partners need access to a specific dataset

## Key expiration

You can set an expiration date when creating a key. The key works through the whole of that day (UTC) and stops at the start of the next one. After that, the key no longer authenticates and requests signed with it fail with a `403` (typically `AccessDenied` or `InvalidAccessKeyId`).

Expiring keys are useful for:
- Temporary access grants
- CI/CD pipelines where you rotate credentials on a schedule
- Short-lived integrations

## Viewing and managing keys

Go to **API Keys** in the left sidebar to see your keys. The list shows:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| Name | The label you gave the key at creation, with the Access Key ID shown beneath it |
| Region | The region the key belongs to (hidden on narrow screens) |
| Buckets | Which buckets the key can access (all, or a specific set) |
| Permissions | The object permissions as badges, and a **+***n* badge for the rest |
| Created by | Who created the key, and who rotated it and when. Shown when your organization has more than one member |
| Status | **Active**, or **Expired** once the expiry date has passed |

Click a key's row to see its expiry date, region, buckets, and full permissions. The console doesn't show when a key was last used, so name keys after what uses them. You cannot view the Secret Access Key after creation. See [API Keys in the console](https://docs.filone.com/app/api-keys#the-key-list) for search, filters, and deleting several keys at once.

## Rotating a key

Rotation gives a key a new Access Key ID and Secret Access Key and keeps everything else: its name, permissions, bucket scope, region, and expiry date.

1. Find the key in **API Keys**, open its **⋯** action menu, and choose **Rotate**.
2. Confirm with **Rotate key** in the **Rotate access key** dialog.
3. Copy or download the new credentials from the **Save your credentials** dialog. As at creation, the secret is shown only once.

The old secret stops working as soon as the new one is issued, so update your applications right away. If the old key couldn't be revoked, the console tells you it is still active; delete it from the list yourself.

You can't rotate an expired key; create a new one instead. **Rotate** only appears on keys your current role could still create.

To move an application onto a key with different permissions or buckets, create the new key, switch the application over, then delete the old key.

## Revoking a key

Find the key in **API Keys**, open its **⋯** action menu, and choose **Delete**. A deleted key can't be restored. Anything that uses it loses access, so switch your applications to another key first. The key stays in your list until its revocation is confirmed. Treat revocation as taking effect quickly rather than at a guaranteed instant.

## Security best practices

- **Use separate keys per environment.** Create different keys for development, staging, and production. This limits the impact if a key is leaked.
- **Use the minimum permissions required.** A key that only needs to read objects should not have Write or Delete permissions.
- **Scope keys to specific buckets** when possible, especially for external integrations.
- **Set expiration dates** on keys that are only needed temporarily.
- **Rotate keys periodically.** Use **Rotate** on the key, then update your application with the new credentials. See [Rotating a key](#rotating-a-key).
- **Revoke keys immediately** if you suspect compromise, and rotate anything that depended on them. Treat revocation as effective quickly rather than assuming a precise cut-off instant.
- **Never hardcode credentials** in source code. Use environment variables or a secrets manager, and keep downloaded `.env` and `.csv` credential files out of version control.
- **Don't paste keys into AI tools.** Give a coding agent its own narrowly scoped key in a named profile instead. See [Use with an AI Agent](https://docs.filone.com/sdk/ai-agents).

See [Authentication](https://docs.filone.com/security/authentication) for how to configure your S3 client with your API keys.


---

# Encryption

Source: https://docs.filone.com/security/encryption

Fil One encrypts all data by default. There is nothing to configure — encryption is always on.

## Encryption at rest

All objects stored in Fil One are encrypted at rest. Encryption is applied automatically when data is written and decrypted automatically when data is read. You do not need to set any headers or configure any options, and it cannot be disabled.

Encryption is performed by the S3 storage gateway for the region your bucket lives in, not by the Fil One console. This applies to all objects in all buckets, with no exceptions.

**Do not send encryption headers.** Fil One applies its own server-side encryption, and you cannot request a specific mode. Uploads specifying `ServerSideEncryption: aws:kms` (SSE-KMS) are **rejected in both regions**: with `InvalidRequest` in `us-east-1`, and with `AccessDenied` or `InvalidRequest` in `eu-west-1` depending on the operation (`PutObject`, `CopyObject`, and `CreateMultipartUpload` are all affected). SSE-C headers are rejected in `eu-west-1`; this is not yet confirmed in `us-east-1`, so don't send them there either. Omit encryption headers entirely: encryption is applied either way.

The bucket-level encryption operations (`GetBucketEncryption`, `PutBucketEncryption`, `DeleteBucketEncryption`) can't be granted to any access key, in either region, so there is no encryption configuration to read or change over the API. Encryption is still always on.

## Encryption in transit

All connections to the regional endpoints (`https://s3.eu-west-1.filonecontent.com`, `https://s3.us-east-1.filonecontent.com`) use **TLS**. HTTP connections are rejected. Your data is always encrypted during transmission between your application and the Fil One endpoint.

This applies to all API operations, including uploads, downloads, presigned URLs, and metadata requests.

## Key management

Encryption keys are held by the **regional storage operator** that fulfils storage for your bucket's region, not by Fil One and not by you. You do not supply or manage encryption keys, and there is no customer-managed-key option.

If your compliance requirements depend on the specific cipher in use, or on who holds key material for a given region, [contact support](https://docs.filone.com/app/support) — those details are set by the regional operator rather than by Fil One.

## Client-side encryption

If your security requirements call for client-side encryption (encrypting data before it reaches the network), encrypt the bytes in your own application before uploading. Note that AWS's dedicated **S3 Encryption Client** exists only for some SDKs (Java, .NET, Go, Ruby) — **boto3, the AWS CLI, and the JavaScript SDK v3 do not provide one** — so with Python, the CLI, or JavaScript you must handle encryption yourself with a standard crypto library. Fil One stores whatever bytes you send: if you encrypt client-side, the stored object is the encrypted blob.

Client-side encryption is optional and is in addition to the server-side encryption that Fil One applies automatically.


---

# Trial & Billing

Source: https://docs.filone.com/billing/trial

## Free trial

Every new account starts with a 30-day free trial. No credit card is required. The trial starts once you have verified your email address.

Each person gets **one trial**, on the first organization they own. Changing your email address does not grant a second one. Members invited to someone else's organization do not get a trial of their own.
