An organization you create after your first has **no trial**: it needs a payment method before you can use it, and it is billed separately, with its own $5.99 / month minimum.

| Included | Amount |
|----------|--------|
| Storage | 1 TB (1,000 GB) |
| Egress bandwidth | 2 TB (2,000 GB) |
| API operations | Unlimited |
| Duration | 30 days from when the trial starts |

The trial gives you enough capacity to test real workloads, not just sample uploads. Almost everything works during the trial; the two exceptions are generating **shareable links** for objects and viewing **invoice history**, both of which unlock on a paid plan.

Warning: Trial caps are enforced, and the two caps behave differently
The storage and egress figures above are hard limits, not soft allowances, and reaching them has different consequences:

- **Storage reaching 1 TB** puts the account into a **write-locked** state — you can still read and download, but new uploads are rejected.
- **Egress reaching 2 TB** **disables the account** — the same state as an account whose grace period has ended, with no read or write access until you upgrade. There is no read-only grace period first.

Trial egress is a **single cumulative budget** across the whole 30 days, not a monthly amount that resets. Enforcement runs on a twice-daily usage job (around 07:00 and 19:00 UTC), so a cap may be exceeded for a few hours before access changes.

## What happens when the trial ends

| Phase | Days | What you can do |
|-------|------|-----------------|
| **Active trial** | 0-30 | Full access. Upload, download, manage data. |
| **Grace period** | 31-37 | **Read-only.** Download your data and upgrade to a paid plan. No new uploads. |
| **Expired** | 38+ | Account disabled. No access to data, uploads, or API keys. An Owner can still reactivate from **Billing**. |

The trial ends at the end of day 30, but the read-only state is applied by a job that runs twice a day (08:00 and 20:00 UTC). Uploads over the S3 API can keep working for up to about 12 hours after the trial ends, until that job runs.

You will receive email reminders at:
- **Day 15** -- Halfway through your trial, with an upgrade link.
- **Day 25** -- 5 days left, with an upgrade link.
- **Day 31** -- Trial ended, grace period started.
- **Day 36** -- Grace period ends in 48 hours.
- **Day 38** -- Account disabled.

Note:
You can upgrade to a paid plan at any time during the trial or grace period, and an organization Owner can reactivate from **Billing** after the account is disabled too. Upgrading or reactivating restores full access immediately.

Info: What "disabled" means
Disabling blocks all access to the account: your data is no longer reachable through the API or the dashboard, and access keys stop working. Fil One does not run an automatic purge at this point. To restore access, an organization Owner opens **Billing** and clicks **Reactivate**. To have your data removed, email [support@filone.com](mailto:support@filone.com).

## Paid plan pricing

| Component | Price | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Storage | $5.99 / TB / month | Billed on average daily usage, minimum $5.99 / month. |
| Egress bandwidth | No charge | No egress fees. |
| API operations | Included | No per-request charges. |

Pricing is usage-based, measured as the average storage consumed across the billing period, with a **$5.99 / month minimum**. If your usage works out to less than $5.99 in a billing period, you are billed the $5.99 minimum. Organizations that subscribed before the move to $5.99 keep their earlier terms; see [Pricing](https://docs.filone.com/billing/pricing). **Pay as you go** has no contract or term commitment. For volume pricing on 1, 3, or 5-year terms, the **Business plan** is arranged with the sales team. See [Billing](https://docs.filone.com/app/billing#choosing-a-plan).

## Payment

Payments are processed through Stripe. An organization Owner adds a credit card from Billing in the dashboard, opened from **Billing** under **Organization** in the left sidebar. See [Billing](https://docs.filone.com/app/billing).

- Invoices are generated monthly.
- Usage details are visible on the Billing page to Owners and Admins.
- Each invoice is charged automatically to the card on file.

## Payment failures

If a payment fails, your account enters **past due** status and Stripe automatically retries the charge. The **dashboard becomes read-only** from the moment the payment fails, and the Billing page shows **Your last payment failed** with an **Update payment** button.

If all retries are exhausted and the subscription is canceled by Stripe, your account transitions to the paid grace period (see below).

Warning: Check the Billing page, not your inbox
Don't rely on an email to tell you a payment has failed. If uploads stop working, open **Billing** in the dashboard: a **Your last payment failed** banner means the card needs updating, and an Owner can fix it with **Update payment**. See [Billing](https://docs.filone.com/app/billing#your-plan).

## Cancellation

An organization Owner can cancel the paid plan from the **Stripe billing portal**, which opens from **Billing** in the dashboard. Admins can see usage on Billing but can't open the portal. When cancellation takes effect depends on the option you choose there: if you cancel at the end of the current billing period, your plan stays **active and billable until that period ends**. The **30-day grace period** begins only once Stripe actually cancels the subscription — not the moment you click cancel:

| Phase | Duration | What you can do |
|-------|----------|-----------------|
| **Grace period** | 30 days | **Read-only.** Download your data or reactivate your plan. No new uploads. |
| **Expired** | After grace period | Account disabled. No access to data, uploads, or API keys. |

Reactivating restores full access immediately, during the grace period or after the account is disabled: an organization Owner opens **Billing** and clicks **Reactivate**. Reactivating starts a new subscription, so your billing date moves to the day you reactivate. To have your data removed instead, email [support@filone.com](mailto:support@filone.com).


---

# Pricing

Source: https://docs.filone.com/billing/pricing

Fil One is priced at **$5.99 / TB / month**, with a **$5.99 / month minimum**. If you store less than 1 TB, you are billed the $5.99 minimum.

No egress fees, no per-request charges, no hidden costs.

This is the self-service **Pay as you go** plan. For volume pricing on 1, 3, or 5-year terms, the **Business plan** is arranged with the sales team. See [Billing](https://docs.filone.com/app/billing#choosing-a-plan).

## How billing is calculated

Your bill is based on the average amount of data you store over the billing period:

- Stored bytes are measured as daily readings and averaged across the billing period. A metering job reports the running average **twice a day** (around 07:00 and 19:00 UTC).
- Storage is charged at a single flat rate of **$5.99 per TB per month**, applied to your average usage, with a **$5.99 / month minimum**. Any period that works out to less than $5.99 is billed at the $5.99 minimum. There is no separate "first TB" tier — it is one linear rate plus a floor.

Storage is measured precisely and in **decimal** units (1 TB = 1,000 GB), so you are billed for what you actually store rather than being rounded up to the next whole TB.

### Examples

Illustrative figures for a steady amount stored for the full month, at $5.99 per TB with the $5.99 monthly minimum applied:

| Average stored | Monthly bill |
|----------------|--------------|
| 500 GB | $5.99 (minimum applies) |
| 1 TB (1,000 GB) | ~$5.99 |
| 1.5 TB (1,500 GB) | ~$8.99 |
| 2 TB (2,000 GB) | ~$11.98 |

Note:
These figures are illustrative. Your invoice is the source of truth for exact amounts — open the **Billing** page in the dashboard to see your current usage and charges.

If the amount you store changes during the month, it is averaged first. For example, storing 2 TB for the first 10 days and 0.5 TB for the remaining 20 days averages to 1 TB, billed at $5.99 for that month.

Note: If your account predates the current price
These are the prices for new customers. Organizations that subscribed before the move to $5.99 keep their earlier terms: $4.99 / TB / month with a $4.99 / month minimum, or, for accounts created before any monthly minimum was introduced, per-unit pricing with no minimum. The **Billing** page shows your own rate.


---

# Usage

Source: https://docs.filone.com/billing/usage

The **Billing** page in the dashboard shows your current usage for the active billing period. It is visible to organization Owners and Admins. See [Billing](https://docs.filone.com/app/billing).

## What is measured

| Metric | How it's measured |
|--------|------------------|
| **Storage** | Average daily storage across the billing period, in GB or TB |
| **Egress bandwidth** | Total data downloaded from Fil One in the billing period |

Storage is measured as an average rather than a peak — if you store 2 TB for half the month and 1 TB for the other half, you are billed for 1.5 TB. Fil One counts storage in **decimal** units: 1 TB is 1,000 GB, and 1 GB is 1,000,000,000 bytes.

**On a paid plan, egress is not charged** — there are no egress fees. During the trial, egress is capped (see below).

You may see three egress figures. **Billing** shows egress for the current billing period. The **Dashboard** shows a rolling 30-day total. The trial cap counts egress cumulatively from the day the trial started.

## Trial limits

During the free trial, usage is capped at:
- **Storage — 1 TB (1,000 GB):** reaching this limit **write-locks** the account. You can still read and download; new uploads are rejected. If you delete data and your storage drops back under 1 TB, the write lock lifts on the next usage run.
- **Egress — 2 TB (2,000 GB), cumulative over the whole trial:** reaching this limit **disables** the account entirely — no read or write access — the same state as an account whose grace period has ended, with no read-only grace period first. This is a single budget for the full 30 days, not a monthly amount that resets.

These caps are enforced by a usage job that runs **twice a day** (around 07:00 and 19:00 UTC), so you may exceed a cap for a few hours before the account state changes — there is no real-time block at the exact moment you cross it. Upgrading to a paid plan removes both caps immediately.

## Versioning and storage costs

If versioning is enabled on a bucket, every version of an object counts as stored storage. Overwriting a 1 GB file 10 times results in 10 GB of stored versions. Consider deleting old versions you no longer need to reduce storage costs. See [Versioning](https://docs.filone.com/storage/versioning).

## Billing period

Paid accounts are billed monthly. The billing period resets on the same day each month (the date you upgraded from the trial, or the date you last reactivated). Usage resets at the start of each new billing period.

See [Trial & Billing](https://docs.filone.com/billing/trial) for pricing details.


---

# App: Dashboard

Source: https://docs.filone.com/app/dashboard

The dashboard at [app.filone.com](https://app.filone.com) is the home page of the console, reached from **Dashboard** at the top of the left sidebar. It summarises your plan, usage, and recent activity. A **New bucket** button sits in the header. During the trial, a **Free trial** banner shows the days left and an **Upgrade** button. You can dismiss it with its **×** button.

For sign-in methods, email verification, two-factor authentication, and passkeys, see [Account Security](https://docs.filone.com/security/account-security).

## Get started

A new organization opens on a **Get started** page instead of the dashboard, because its dashboard would be all zeros. The page offers **Create bucket** and **Create API key**, which change to **Create another bucket** and **Create another key** once you have one. Below them, **Explore more** links to inviting your team, these docs, and the Fil One team. The page stays at `/get-started` if you want to come back to it.

## Plan, storage, and egress

Three cards sit below the header. The **PLAN** card is only shown to roles that can view billing (Owner and Admin), so other roles see just the storage and egress cards. See [Roles and permissions](https://docs.filone.com/app/organization#roles-and-permissions).

- **PLAN** shows your plan name and a status badge (**Active**, **Past Due**, **Grace Period**, **Canceled**, or **No plan**). During the trial the badge counts down as *n* **days left**, and hovering it shows the exact expiry time. The footer link goes to Billing.
- **STORAGE** shows how much you are storing. On the trial it adds a **/ 1 TB** suffix and a progress bar. On a paid plan with a per-TB rate it instead shows an **Est. monthly cost** row.
- **EGRESS** shows your egress. On the trial it adds a **/ 2 TB** suffix and a progress bar. On a paid plan it reads **No egress fees · unlimited**.

Below those, a strip shows your **BUCKETS**, **OBJECTS**, and **API KEYS** totals, with **View all** links for buckets and API keys.

Info: How to read these numbers
**Sizes are decimal.** 1 GB means 1,000,000,000 bytes and 1 TB means 1,000 GB, matching how your usage is billed. See [Usage](https://docs.filone.com/billing/usage).

**Storage is the most recent reading**, sampled periodically rather than live, so a change you just made may take a little while to appear.

**Egress is a rolling 30-day total** rather than a calendar-month figure, so it moves with the trailing month instead of resetting on the 1st.

**Est. monthly cost is a guide.** It applies your plan's per-TB price to your latest storage reading, with your monthly minimum as the floor. It is not shown when your plan has no per-TB rate. Your invoice is calculated from your average storage across the month, so expect the two to differ. See [Pricing](https://docs.filone.com/billing/pricing).

## Usage Trends

**Usage Trends** charts your history over a **7 days** or **30 days** window, defaulting to 7. **Storage** is an area chart, and the figure above it is the most recent reading. **Egress** is a bar chart, and the figure above it is the total egress across the window.

Each point is a daily reading. Days without a reading are plotted as zero, so a gap in the data appears as a dip to zero.

## Recent Activity

**Recent Activity** lists your five most recent events, each with a relative timestamp such as `5m ago` or `2d ago`.

The feed currently covers bucket and key creation. Each row shows the resource name with a **bucket** or **key** badge and the label **Created**. Object-level events are not included yet, so open a bucket to confirm an upload rather than looking for it here. With no activity yet the card reads **No activity yet** and offers a **Create bucket** button.

## Account state banners

When your account is restricted, a banner appears above the page on every screen, not just the dashboard:

| Situation | What the banner says |
|-----------|----------------------|
| Trial storage cap reached | **Storage limit exceeded. Uploads are disabled. Delete files or upgrade to resume.** |
| Trial expired, in grace period | That the trial has expired, with the days left to upgrade or download your data |
| Account disabled | **Account disabled. Visit billing to restore access.** |

Roles that cannot view billing see a shorter banner that leaves out the cause: when writes are paused it says uploads are disabled for this organization, and when the account is disabled it says so. Both ask you to contact an organization owner.

Reads keep working while writes are paused, so your data stays available to download throughout. See [Trial & Billing](https://docs.filone.com/billing/trial) for the full lifecycle and [Usage](https://docs.filone.com/billing/usage) for how the caps are applied.


---

# App: Buckets

Source: https://docs.filone.com/app/buckets

**Buckets** in the left sidebar is where you create buckets and work with their contents without writing code.

This page covers the console specifically. For the concepts, the S3 API equivalents, and code samples, see [Buckets](https://docs.filone.com/storage/buckets), [Objects](https://docs.filone.com/storage/objects), [Versioning](https://docs.filone.com/storage/versioning), and [Object Lock](https://docs.filone.com/storage/object-lock).

## The bucket list

The table shows **Name**, **Region** (both the label and the region ID, such as Europe (France) and `eu-west-1`), and **Created**. Under each name a second line gives the bucket's storage used and object count, and an icon marks the bucket as private.

All of your buckets are listed together, sorted by name. Once you have 5 or more buckets, a **Search buckets** box appears above the table, the column headers become sortable, and a region filter appears when your buckets span more than one region. With no buckets yet the page reads **No buckets yet** and offers **Create bucket**.

If one region cannot be reached, an amber notice names it and the buckets in the other regions are still listed.

Each row has an actions menu with **Browse objects**, **Copy bucket name**, **Copy S3 endpoint**, and **Delete bucket**.

### Deleting a bucket

Warning: Deleting a bucket can't be undone
A deleted bucket can't be restored, and applications that use it start failing straight away.

Choose **Delete bucket** from the row's actions menu and confirm. Only empty buckets can be deleted: if the bucket still holds objects or object versions, the console says it is not empty and links to how to empty it. Use [Empty bucket](#emptying-a-bucket) first, then delete.

**Delete bucket** is only shown to Owners and Admins. It works in every region, including `eu-west-1`, where `DeleteBucket` is not available over the S3 API. See [Buckets](https://docs.filone.com/storage/buckets#deleting-a-bucket).

## Creating a bucket

Click **Create bucket** (or **New bucket** on the Dashboard) and fill in:

1. **Bucket name.** 3 to 63 characters, lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only, starting and ending with a letter or number. No dots, unlike AWS S3. The form says it "must be unique in this region".
2. **Region.** Europe (France) `eu-west-1`, the default, or US East (Michigan) `us-east-1`. This sets the endpoint you connect to.
3. **Advanced settings**, collapsed by default because most buckets don't need them. Expand it to set three switches that build on one another, all off by default:
   - **Versioning** keeps multiple versions of an object.
   - **Object Lock** can't be turned on until Versioning is, and shows a **Needs Versioning** badge until then.
   - **Retention** can't be turned on until Object Lock is, and shows a **Needs Object Lock** badge until then. Turning it on reveals a **Default Retention Policy** with **Governance** or **Compliance** mode (Governance by default) and a **Lock period** in **Days** or **Years**, defaulting to 15 days. The maximum is 100 years.

   Turning a switch back off resets the ones that depend on it. While the section is collapsed, the line beside it lists what is on.

Click **Create bucket**. The console opens the new bucket, and its empty state offers **Create API key** (or **View API keys**, if you already have keys that reach it) so you can connect an application.

A panel headed **Included by default** confirms two things you do not configure: all data is encrypted at rest, and every bucket is private, so access requires an API key.

Warning: These choices are permanent
Name, region, versioning, Object Lock, and the default retention policy are all fixed when the bucket is created, in the console and over the API alike. Decide on them up front, and create a new bucket if you later need a different configuration.

## Inside a bucket

Opening a bucket shows its region and storage used, then three property cards: **Versioning** and **Object Lock** (each **Enabled** or **Disabled**), and **Retention**, which shows the default retention policy, such as **Compliance · 15 days**, or **None**. Encryption is on for every bucket, so it has no card of its own.

Once the bucket holds objects, **Empty bucket** and **Upload object** buttons appear in the header. While it is empty, the upload button sits in the empty state instead.

Two tabs follow:

- **Objects (N)** is the object browser.
- **API Keys (N)** lists the keys that can reach this bucket, plus an **Access endpoints** block with the copyable **S3 Endpoint**, **S3 Path**, and **Region** you need to configure a client. This tab is hidden for the Read-only role.

### Browsing objects

The object table shows **Name**, **Size**, and **Last Modified**, plus **Version** and **Status** columns when versioning is enabled. Keys containing `/` are grouped into folder rows you can click into, with a breadcrumb to walk back out.

On a versioned bucket, a key with more than one version gets an expander and an *n* **versions** pill. Expanding shows the older versions, badged **Latest** for the current one and **Delete marker** where a delete marker sits on top.

Per-row icon buttons download, share, or delete a single object. A checkbox on each row, and on the header, lets you select several at once. See [Deleting objects](#deleting-objects).

Note: Large buckets
The browser shows the first page of results, around 1,000 entries. When there are more, an amber **Showing the first** *n* notice appears, and selecting and deleting apply only to the objects listed. The count on the **Objects (N)** tab then comes from your bucket analytics, a daily reading that can lag recent changes, so expect it to be higher than the number of rows in view. Use the AWS CLI or an SDK to page through a full listing, or [Empty bucket](#emptying-a-bucket) to remove everything. See [Objects](https://docs.filone.com/storage/objects).

## Uploading

Open a bucket and click **Upload object**. You can drag files or whole folders onto the drop zone, or use **Select files** and **Select folder**.

An optional **Prefix** field puts your files under a path such as `images/`. Two details are worth knowing:

- The prefix field appears when you select individual files. Files picked as a folder keep their own relative paths, which take the place of the prefix.
- The prefix starts empty each time rather than carrying over from the folder you were browsing, so set it on every upload where you want one.

Folder uploads skip system files that come along with a folder: `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`, `desktop.ini`, anything whose path contains a segment starting with a dot, and `__MACOSX` folders. A **Skipped** *n* **system files** message tells you how many were left out. A file you select on its own is always uploaded, whatever its name.

Selecting files does not upload them. Click **Upload** *n* **file(s)** to start, and a per-run progress bar tracks the batch. If any file fails, a **Retry** *n* **failed** button retries just those rather than the whole set.

Note: Object size
The console uploads each file in a single request, which the S3 single-PUT ceiling caps at 5 GB. For objects above that, use the AWS CLI or an SDK with multipart support. See [Multipart Uploads](https://docs.filone.com/storage/multipart-uploads).

## The object detail page

Clicking an object shows its **Name**, **Size**, **Bucket**, **S3 Path**, **ETag**, and, where they apply, **Version ID**, **Retention**, **Description**, and **Tags**. **Description** and **Tags** are read from the object's `description` and `tags` user metadata, not from S3 object tagging, and the console upload flow does not set them. When retention is in Compliance mode a **Compliance retention lock** notice gives the date before which the object cannot be deleted.

A **Version history** card appears when the object has more than one version, listing each **Version ID** with its **Status**, **Size**, and **Last Modified**, and marking the one you are viewing. Clicking another row opens that version.

Note: Working with versions
Version history is drawn from the object list you arrived through, so open the bucket first if you have followed a direct link to an object and the card is not showing.

To bring an earlier version back as the current one, download it and upload it again. See [Versioning](https://docs.filone.com/storage/versioning).

## Downloading and sharing

**Download** is available on each row in the object list and in the object detail header. It works on any plan, including the trial.

**Share object** generates a link anyone can open without an API key. Choose an expiry of **1 hour**, **24 hours** (the default), **3 days**, or **7 days**, then **Generate link**.

Sharing is a paid-plan feature. During the trial the button is disabled, with a tooltip pointing to an upgrade.

## Deleting objects

Click the trash icon on a row, or **Delete object** on the detail page, and confirm.

To delete several at once, tick their checkboxes. A bar shows *n* **selected** with **Clear** and **Delete**. Ticking a folder row selects everything under it, and the header checkbox selects everything at the current level.

Warning: Console deletes are permanent, including on versioned buckets
The console always deletes the specific version on the row you chose. It does not write a delete marker. On a versioned bucket, deleting the row for the current version permanently removes that version, and the earlier versions are left as they are. To hide an object behind a delete marker instead, delete it over the S3 API without a version ID. See [Versioning](https://docs.filone.com/storage/versioning#delete-markers).

An object under an active retention period or legal hold is protected, and attempting to delete it returns that protection as an error. See [Object Lock](https://docs.filone.com/storage/object-lock).

### Emptying a bucket

Danger: Empty bucket permanently deletes everything in the bucket
It removes every object, every earlier version, and every delete marker that isn't protected by retention or a legal hold. It can't be undone, and versioning doesn't protect you: nothing is kept to restore from.

**Empty bucket** on the bucket page removes every object in the bucket, including every earlier version and delete marker. Type the bucket name to confirm, then click **Delete everything**.

The deletion runs on the server, so it is not limited to the objects listed on screen, and it keeps running if you close the dialog. When it finishes, the dialog reports **Bucket empty**, **Some objects remain** (with how many could not be deleted, for example because they are under active retention), or **Deletion stopped** if the job could not complete.

Deleting objects, in bulk or one at a time, and emptying a bucket all need a role that can delete objects. Uploading and creating buckets need a role that can write objects and create buckets. Controls you cannot use are hidden, and opening the upload or create page directly explains that the action is not part of your role. See [Roles and permissions](https://docs.filone.com/app/organization#roles-and-permissions).

While an account is past due or in a grace period, access is read-only and uploads and deletions resume once the payment succeeds. See [Trial & Billing](https://docs.filone.com/billing/trial).


---

# App: API Keys

Source: https://docs.filone.com/app/api-keys

**API Keys** in the left sidebar is where you create the S3 credentials your tools and code use.

This page covers the console specifically. For what each permission allows, how signing works, and security guidance, see [API Keys](https://docs.filone.com/security/api-keys) and [Authentication](https://docs.filone.com/security/authentication).

## The key list

The page has two tabs, **API keys** and **Connection details**. The table shows:

| Column | What it holds |
|--------|---------------|
| **Name** | The key name, with the Access Key ID underneath and a copy button |
| **Region** | The region the key belongs to, such as `eu-west-1` (hidden on narrow screens) |
| **Buckets** | **All Buckets**, or one badge per bucket the key is scoped to |
| **Permissions** | Badges for the object permissions (**Read**, **Write**, **List**, **Delete**), and a **+***n* badge for the rest. Open the key to see them all |
| **Created by** | The member who created the key, and **Rotated by … on …** once it has been rotated. Shown when your organization has more than one member |
| **Status** | **Active**, or **Expired** once the key's expiry date has passed |
| **⋯** | **Rotate** and **Delete**, for the keys you can act on |

With 5 or more keys, a **Search keys** box (by name or Access Key ID) and filters for region (**All regions**) and status (**All statuses**) appear above the table.

Click a key's row to open its details: its **Status**, when it **Expires** (or **Never**), when it was **Created** and **Rotated**, its **Region**, which **Buckets** it reaches ("All buckets in this region" for an unscoped key), and its full **Object permissions** and **Bucket management** permissions. The details panel is the place to check a key's expiry date.

With no keys yet the page reads **No API keys yet** and offers **Create your first key**. A Member sees "You can only see the keys you create. Owners and Admins see every key in the organization." instead, because the organization may hold keys they aren't shown.

If your account is disabled, the **API Keys** page shows only a notice asking you to reactivate your subscription, with no keys, tabs, or **Create new key** button.

Note: Name keys for what uses them
The console doesn't show when a key was last used. Give each key a descriptive name, such as `backup-job-prod`, so you can tell from the list which application would break if you deleted it.

## Who can manage keys

What you can do here depends on your [role](https://docs.filone.com/app/organization#roles-and-permissions):

- **Read only** members cannot create keys. The **API keys** tab explains that keys are managed by members who can create them, and the **Connection details** tab is still available.
- **Members** see, rotate, and delete only the keys they created themselves.
- **Admins** and **Owners** see and manage every key in the organization.

A key can only carry permissions your role holds, and the form hides the ones it doesn't. **Set retention** and **Set legal hold** are Owner-only, so they appear only for Owners. If a member's role is narrowed, any key they created that the new role couldn't create is revoked, and removing a member revokes the keys they created. The member is emailed a list of the revoked keys. See [Organization](https://docs.filone.com/app/organization#removing-a-member).

## Creating a key

Click **Create new key**, which opens a dedicated page.

**Key name.** Up to 64 characters, using letters, numbers, spaces, underscores, hyphens, and periods. Names must be unique within a region, and names starting with `filone-console` (in any capitalization) are reserved.

**Region.** Required, and pre-set to `eu-west-1`. A key is scoped to the region you pick, and each region has its own endpoint, so the endpoint, the region, and the key all need to agree. If you store data in both regions, create a key for each.

**What can this key do?** Object permissions are:

| Permission | Allows |
|------------|--------|
| **Read** | Download and retrieve objects |
| **Write** | Upload and overwrite objects |
| **List** | Browse and list objects |
| **Delete** | Permanently remove objects |

**Read**, **Write**, and **List** are pre-selected. **Delete** is not. For a read-only key, untick **Write**: a key with **Write** can overwrite any object it reaches.

Checking one of those reveals finer-grained permissions nested underneath it. These are granted individually, so tick the ones you need:

- Under **Read**: **Read object versions**, **Read retention settings**, **Read legal hold status**
- Under **Write**: **Set retention**, **Set legal hold**
- Under **List**: **List object versions**
- Under **Delete**: **Delete object versions**

A key with **Write** therefore needs **Set retention** ticked as well before it can apply a retention policy. Unchecking a parent clears whatever was nested under it.

**Bucket management** is a separate section:

- **List all buckets** is always on.
- **Read bucket versioning** and **Read object lock configuration** are available in every region, and both are pre-selected.
- **Create bucket** and **Delete bucket** are available in the regions that support bucket management over the S3 API. In `eu-west-1`, the default region, they are disabled with the tooltip **Not supported in Europe (France)**, and you create buckets in the console instead.

**Which buckets can this key access?** Defaults to **All buckets**, meaning every bucket in the key's region. Choose **Specific buckets** to pick from a list, filtered to the region you selected.

**When should it expire?** **Never expires** (the default), **30 days**, or **Custom** with a date picker. A key with an expiry date works through the whole of that day (UTC) and stops at the start of the next one.

Click **Create API key** to create it.

## Saving the secret

On success a **Save your credentials** dialog shows the **Access Key ID** and the **Secret Access Key**, with the secret masked until you reveal it. You can copy either, or download the pair as a `.csv` or `.env` file.

A downloaded file holds the secret in plain text. Move the values into your password manager, secrets store, or your tool's credential file, then delete the download. Never commit it: if you keep a `.env` in a project, add it to `.gitignore` first.

Warning: The secret is shown once
Fil One never stores your secret, which is why it appears only when a key is created or rotated. Copy or download it before closing the dialog. If you lose it, [rotate the key](#rotating-a-key) to get a new secret.

## Rotating a key

Open the **⋯** menu on the key's row and choose **Rotate**. The **Rotate access key** dialog explains that the key keeps its name, permissions, and buckets, and gets a new Access Key ID and secret. Its region and expiry date carry over too. Confirm with **Rotate key**, and the **Save your credentials** dialog opens with the new pair, shown once as at creation.

The old secret stops working as soon as the new one is issued, so update anything that uses the key. If the old key can't be revoked, a message says the new credentials are ready but the key they replace is still active. Delete the old key from the list yourself in that case.

A few limits apply:

- An expired key can't be rotated. Create a new key instead.
- **Rotate** only appears on keys your current role could still create. See [Who can manage keys](#who-can-manage-keys).

After a rotation, the **Created by** column shows who rotated the key and when.

## Revoking a key

Warning: Deleting a key breaks anything that uses it
A deleted key stops working immediately and can't be restored. To move an application onto a key with different permissions or buckets, create the new key first, switch the application over, then delete the old one.

Open the **⋯** menu on the key's row and choose **Delete**. The dialog warns that the key will be permanently revoked and that any application using it loses access immediately. Deleting a key is how you revoke it.

To delete several keys at once, tick their checkboxes (or the header checkbox). A bar shows *n* **selected** with **Clear** and **Delete**. Only keys you're allowed to delete can be selected.

A key stays in your list until its revocation is confirmed, so a key that is still listed is a key that still works.

Note: Keys for a bucket
A bucket's **API Keys** tab shows the keys that can reach that bucket, which is a quicker way to audit access for one bucket than reading down the full list.


---

# App: Organization

Source: https://docs.filone.com/app/organization

Every Fil One account starts as a one-person organization, with you as its **Owner**. You can invite teammates, give each one a role, and see what has changed in the organization.

## Where to find the organization's pages

The organization's pages are in the **Organization** group of the left sidebar. You only see the entries your role can open:

| Entry | What it opens | Who sees it |
|-------|---------------|-------------|
| **Members** | Everyone in the organization, and pending invitations (see [Members](#members)) | Every role |
| **Billing** | Your plan, usage, payment method, and invoices (see [Billing](https://docs.filone.com/app/billing)) | Owner, Admin |
| **Audit log** | A record of membership, key, and organization changes (see [Audit log](#audit-log)) | Owner, Admin |

The organization's logo and name sit at the top of the left sidebar. Click them to open the **organization menu**, which holds:

- **Edit organization**, for Owners and Admins: the organization's name and logo, and how to delete it (see [Editing the organization](#editing-the-organization))
- your organizations, if you belong to more than one (see [Switching organizations](#switching-organizations))
- **Create organization**, for every role (see [Creating another organization](#creating-another-organization))

Each page has its own address: `/edit-organization`, `/members`, `/billing`, and `/audit`.

While an organization has no active plan, every page except Settings, Edit organization, and Support is replaced by **Add a payment method to continue**, and the sidebar's page links are hidden until a plan is in place. See [Billing](https://docs.filone.com/app/billing).

## Editing the organization

**Edit organization**, for Owners and Admins, opens a page with two sections:

- **General** holds the organization's logo and **Organization name**. A new logo saves as soon as it uploads. A new name needs **Save**, and must be 2 to 100 characters, using letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, and periods only. Every member sees the change.
- **Danger zone**, shown to Owners only, covers deleting the organization (see [Deleting an organization](#deleting-an-organization)).

Members and Read only members who open the page see "Organization details are managed by your organization's owners and admins."

## Creating another organization

**Create organization** in the organization menu opens a dialog asking for an **Organization name**, with the same rules as above, and an optional logo. You become the new organization's Owner, and the console switches to it straight away. A new organization has its own members, keys, buckets, and billing, separate from the organization you created it from. You can own up to **10** organizations. Organizations you were invited into don't count toward that.

Warning: A new organization has no free trial
Each person gets one [free trial](https://docs.filone.com/billing/trial), on the first organization they own. An organization you create after that has no trial: it shows **Add a payment method to continue** until you add one, and it is billed separately, with its own monthly minimum. See [Pricing](https://docs.filone.com/billing/pricing).

## Roles and permissions

Every member holds exactly one of four roles. The role picker describes them like this:

| Role | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Owner** | Can do everything, including billing and owning the organization. |
| **Admin** | Can manage members, buckets, and keys, but not billing or owners. |
| **Member** | Can read and write objects, and create buckets and their own keys. |
| **Read only** | Can read buckets and objects, but can't make changes. |

The full set of capabilities:

| Capability | Owner | Admin | Member | Read only |
|------------|:-----:|:-----:|:------:|:---------:|
| See the member list | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Invite members, change roles, and remove members (Admin and below) | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| Make someone an Owner, change an Owner's role, or remove an Owner | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Transfer ownership | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Rename the organization | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| View billing (plan, usage, invoices) | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| Manage billing (plan, payment method, Stripe portal) | ✅ | — | — | — |
| View and export the audit log | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| List buckets and read their settings | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Create buckets | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| Delete buckets | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| View and download objects | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Upload objects | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| Delete objects | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| Create access keys | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| See and revoke the keys you created | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| See and revoke every key in the organization | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| Create keys with the `PutObjectRetention` or `PutObjectLegalHold` permission | ✅ | — | — | — |

Read only members don't see **API Keys** in the sidebar, because they can't create or manage keys.

Note: Roles apply in the console. Access keys carry their own permissions.
The S3 API has no users or roles. A request made with an access key is allowed or refused by that key's own permissions and [bucket scope](https://docs.filone.com/security/api-keys#bucket-scope), whoever created it. What keeps keys in line with roles is a cap at creation: a key can only carry permissions its creator's role holds. For example, a Member can't create a key with `DeleteBucket`, and only an Owner can create one with `PutObjectRetention` or `PutObjectLegalHold`. When a member's role narrows, keys that go beyond the new role are revoked (see [Changing a role](#changing-a-role)).

## Members

**Members** in the sidebar opens a page headed **Members**, "People with access to this organization." It has up to two tabs, each with a count beside its label:

| Tab | What it holds | Who sees it |
|-----|---------------|-------------|
| **Members** | Everyone in the organization and their role | Every role |
| **Invitations** | Invitations that have been sent but not yet accepted | Owner, Admin |

Owners and Admins also get an **Add member** button beside the heading, which opens the invitation form (see [Invitations](#invitations)).

The **Members** tab lists everyone in the organization:

| Column | What it holds |
|--------|---------------|
| **Member** | The member's name, a **You** badge on your own row, and their user ID underneath |
| **Role** | A role picker, if you can change this member's role, or a role badge otherwise |
| **Joined** | When they joined, with how: **Signed up**, **Original account**, or **Invited** (hidden on narrow screens) |
| **⋯** | **Transfer ownership** and **Remove**, for the members you can act on |

With 5 or more members, a search box and a role filter appear above the table.

### Changing a role

Owners and Admins change a role from the picker in the **Role** column. The picker only offers roles you're allowed to assign: an Admin can move people between Admin, Member, and Read only, but can't change an Owner's role or make anyone an Owner.

- **Making someone an Owner** asks you to confirm first, because they'll be able to manage billing, every member, and the organization itself, including removing you.
- **Moving someone to a role with fewer permissions** opens a preview of their access keys first. Any key that carries more than the new role allows is listed, and the confirm button becomes **Change role and revoke**. Those keys stop working straight away, and the member is emailed a list of them. To keep a client running, create a replacement key with the narrower permissions first, then change the role. Moving someone to Read only revokes every key they created, since Read only can't hold keys.
- **Moving someone to a role with more permissions** takes effect immediately.

You can change your own role too. The dialog warns you if the change takes away your ability to manage members or billing.

### Removing a member

Warning: Removing a member breaks their keys
Every access key the person created stops working the moment you confirm. If an application uses one of their keys, create a replacement key and switch the application to it first.

Choose **Remove** from the row's **⋯** menu and confirm with **Remove member**. The person loses access to the organization, and **every access key they created is revoked**, so anything still using one stops working straight away. Invitations they sent that are still pending are withdrawn too. The person is emailed a list of the keys that were revoked.

Admins can remove Admins, Members, and Read only members. Only an Owner can remove an Owner. Owners and Admins can remove themselves. Members and Read only members can't remove themselves, so ask an Owner or Admin.

### At least one Owner

An organization always keeps at least one Owner. A role change or removal that would leave it with none is refused, and the page shows **An organization keeps at least one owner**. Make someone else an Owner, or [transfer ownership](#transferring-ownership), first.

### Transferring ownership

An Owner can hand the Owner seat to another member with **Transfer ownership** in that member's **⋯** menu.

1. The dialog explains that the other member becomes Owner and **you move to Admin**, and that you can't take ownership back yourself.
2. If any of your access keys carry permissions an Admin can't hold (such as `PutObjectRetention` or `PutObjectLegalHold`), the dialog lists them. They're revoked as part of the transfer.
3. Type the organization's name to confirm, then click **Transfer ownership**. This cannot be undone.

Transferring needs a recent sign-in. If you haven't signed in within the last five minutes, the console sends you through sign-in again, including your two-factor check if you have one set up, and then reopens the dialog.

Billing is not affected: the subscription belongs to the organization, not to the Owner.

## Invitations

Invitations are how anyone else joins your organization. Sending them needs an Owner or Admin role. They're managed from the **Invitations** tab of the [Members](#members) page.

### Sending an invitation

1. Click **Add member** at the top of the **Members** page.
2. Enter the person's **Email address**.
3. Choose a **Role**. Each role is listed with its description, and the list only includes roles you can assign: an Admin can invite Admins, Members, and Read only members, and an Owner can also invite Owners. **Member** is selected by default.
4. Click **Send invitation**.

The person joins as soon as they accept, at the role you chose. The invitation link can only be used once, and expires in **14 days**.

An organization can have at most **25** invitations pending at once. At the limit, revoke one to send another. Inviting an address that already has a pending invitation replaces the old one rather than taking a second slot.

If the invitation was created but the email couldn't be sent, the tab says so and offers **Send again**.

### The Invitations tab

| Column | What it holds |
|--------|---------------|
| **Email** | The address invited, and when |
| **Role** | The role they'll join at |
| **Status** | **Waiting**, **Not delivered** (the email couldn't be sent), or **Expired** |
| **Expires** | When the link stops working (hidden on narrow screens) |

**Revoke** withdraws an invitation, and the link stops working. **Resend** appears on invitations whose email was not delivered. You can only act on invitations for roles you're allowed to assign.

### Accepting an invitation

The invitation email links to `app.filone.com/invite/accept`. If you're not signed in, you're asked to sign in first and then brought back. The page then shows one of these:

| Outcome | What it means |
|---------|---------------|
| **Welcome to** *organization* | You've joined. The page shows your role and what it lets you do, with **Continue to** *organization*. |
| **You're already in** *organization* | You were already a member. |
| **Wrong account signed in** | The invitation was sent to a different address than the one you're signed in with. Log out, sign in with the right address, and open the link again. |
| **Verify your email address first** | Your email isn't verified yet. Verify it, and you're brought back to accept. |
| **This invitation is no longer valid** | The link has already been used, was revoked, or has expired. Ask an administrator for a new invitation. |

## Switching organizations

If you belong to more than one organization, the organization menu lists them under **Organization**, sorted by name, with a check mark on the one you're in. Choosing another switches the console to that organization and opens its dashboard. With only one membership, the list doesn't appear.

The choice is kept per browser tab, so two tabs can be in different organizations at the same time. The sidebar names the organization you're in, so check it before removing people or transferring ownership.

### Leaving an organization

The **Organizations** section of [Settings](https://docs.filone.com/app/settings) lists every organization you belong to, with your role and when you joined. Each row's menu offers **Switch to this organization** and **Leave organization**. Leaving removes your access to that organization and everything in it, and you can only rejoin with a new invitation. The last Owner of an organization can't leave it: make someone else an Owner first (see [At least one Owner](#at-least-one-owner)).

## Audit log

**Audit log** in the sidebar opens a page, for Owners and Admins, that records changes to the organization:

| Column | What it holds |
|--------|---------------|
| **Event** | What happened |
| **Member** | Who did it |
| **Subject** | What it was done to (hidden on narrow screens) |
| **When** | When it happened |

Expand a row to see its details. Filter by date range (**From**, **To**), by event type (**All events** by default), and by member (**Anyone** by default).

Events recorded:

- Organization created, organization renamed, and organization logo updated
- Member invited, invitation revoked, and invitation accepted
- Role changed, member removed, and ownership transferred
- Key created, key deleted, and key rotated
- Audit log exported

**Download CSV** exports the events that match your current filters. An export can hold up to 20,000 rows. A larger one is refused rather than cut short, so narrow the date range or filter by event type or member.

Events are kept for **90 days**. If you ask for a range that reaches further back, the page tells you the older events have been removed.

## Billing

**Billing** in the sidebar opens the billing page, for Owners and Admins. See [Billing](https://docs.filone.com/app/billing).

## Deleting an organization

Deleting an organization is not available in the console yet. The **Danger zone** on the **Edit organization** page, shown to Owners only, points you to [support@filone.com](mailto:support@filone.com): email them to delete the organization.


---

# App: Billing

Source: https://docs.filone.com/app/billing

Billing is a page of its own, at `/billing`. Open it from **Billing** in the **Organization** group of the left sidebar (see [Where to find the organization's pages](https://docs.filone.com/app/organization#where-to-find-the-organizations-pages)).

Billing is visible to **Owners** and **Admins**. Every action on it (choosing or changing a plan, adding or updating a card, opening the Stripe portal) is for **Owners** only, so an Admin sees the same figures without the buttons. Members and Read only users see "Billing is managed by your organization's owners and admins" instead. See [Roles and permissions](https://docs.filone.com/app/organization#roles-and-permissions).

This page covers the console specifically. For the trial lifecycle, the pricing model, and how usage is measured, see [Trial & Billing](https://docs.filone.com/billing/trial), [Pricing](https://docs.filone.com/billing/pricing), and [Usage](https://docs.filone.com/billing/usage).

## Your plan

The **Plan** card names your plan and carries a status badge:

| Status | Badge | Plan name and detail line |
|--------|-------|---------------------------|
| Trial | **Active** (blue) | **Free trial**. The trial's storage and egress limits are on the [usage card](#usage) |
| Paid | **Active** (green) | **Pay as you go**, with your per-TB rate and the renewal date |
| Billed manually | **Active** (green) | The name on your agreement, or **Custom plan**, with **Billed manually** |
| Payment failed | **Payment failed** (amber) | Your plan name, rate, and renewal date, as for a paid plan |
| Grace period | **Grace period** | Your plan name and rate, and how many days until access ends |
| Canceled | **Canceled** | Your plan name and rate, and the date it was canceled |
| No plan | None | **No plan**, with **Choose a plan to start storing data** |

If your plan was set up with the sales team, the card shows the name on your agreement, and **Custom pricing** where there is no single per-TB rate to show. An organization billed manually by the sales team has no payment method to manage in the console.

The button in this card is **Upgrade** on the trial, **Manage plan** on a paid plan (including one whose payment failed), **Reactivate** once the subscription is canceled, and **Choose a plan** during the grace period or with no plan.

A canceled subscription can be restarted at any time: an Owner clicks **Reactivate**, and the banner confirms "Your data is still here." Access returns as soon as the new subscription starts, without contacting support.

A banner above the cards flags a problem with the account:

| Banner | Button |
|--------|--------|
| **Your last payment failed** | **Update payment** |
| **This organization is read-only** (grace period) | **Choose a plan** |
| **This subscription is canceled** | **Reactivate** |

Note: A failed payment makes the dashboard read-only
When a payment fails, the dashboard becomes read-only. Check the banner and update your payment method to resume. See [Trial & Billing](https://docs.filone.com/billing/trial).

## Usage

The usage card is headed **Usage during your trial** on the trial and **Usage this billing period** otherwise, with the dates of the period and how many days are left.

**Storage** always appears. On the trial it is shown against the 1 TB cap with a progress bar; on a paid plan there is no cap, so you see the figure alone.

**Egress** also always appears. On the trial it is shown against the 2 TB cap with a progress bar. On a paid plan it is labelled **Free**, since there are no egress fees.

**Estimated total** appears on a paid plan with a per-TB rate. Where your monthly minimum is higher than your usage, the estimate shows the minimum, captioned **Your monthly minimum**. Plans with custom pricing show no estimate, and the card says the total for the period is in Stripe.

Info: How the estimate is calculated
The estimate applies your plan's per-TB rate to your most recent storage reading, with your monthly minimum as the floor. Your invoice is calculated from your average storage across the billing period, so treat the estimate as a guide to where you are heading rather than the final figure. Egress is not included, since it is free on paid plans.

Sizes here are decimal: 1 TB means 1,000 GB. See [Usage](https://docs.filone.com/billing/usage).

## Payment method

The **Payment method** card shows one of three things:

| What you see | Button |
|--------------|--------|
| **No card on file**, "Needed before your trial ends" | **Add card** |
| The card brand and last four digits, with the expiry date | **Update** |
| **Billed by invoice**, for a paid plan with no card on file | **Manage** |

**Update**, **Manage**, and **Manage plan** open the Stripe customer portal, where the card details are entered and stored. Fil One does not hold your card number.

Note: Cancelling
Cancellation is handled in the Stripe portal, reached through **Manage plan**, so only Owners can cancel.

## Choosing a plan

**Add card**, **Upgrade**, **Choose a plan**, and **Reactivate** open **Choose your plan**, which offers two plans:

- **Pay as you go**, at **$5.99** per TB per month with a $5.99 monthly minimum, no egress fees, and no API request fees. **Upgrade now** takes you to the payment form.
- **Business plan**, with **Custom pricing**, purchased in 1, 3, or 5-year increments, with capacity assurance and deployment SLAs. **Contact sales team** opens a sales contact form.

The payment form takes your card number, expiry, and CVC. **Start subscription** activates the plan.

If you are reactivating and a card is already on file, the **Pay as you go** button reads **Reactivate** and uses that card, with a **Use a different card** link if you would rather enter a new one.

## Invoices

The **Invoices** list shows the date, status, amount, and a **PDF** link for each invoice. Statuses are **Paid**, **Due**, **Void**, and **Unpaid**.

Three things to expect:

- The list does not appear during the trial or with no plan. Before your first invoice it reads **No invoices yet**.
- It shows your 12 most recent issued invoices, including any that are still unpaid. Drafts are not shown.
- **View all** opens the Stripe portal for your full billing history. It appears for Owners only.

## Need help?

The panel beside the cards offers **Billing questions**, which links to **Contact support** for questions about an invoice, a payment, or your plan. On the trial or with no plan, it also offers **Volume pricing**, where **Talk to sales** opens the sales contact form.

Note: If your account predates the current price
Organizations that subscribed before the move to $5.99 keep their earlier terms: $4.99 per TB with a $4.99 monthly minimum, or, for accounts created before any minimum was introduced, per-unit pricing with no minimum. The plan card and the estimate use your own rate and minimum. The **Choose your plan** dialog always shows the current $5.99 wording, so take the plan card as the guide to your own terms. See [Pricing](https://docs.filone.com/billing/pricing).


---

# App: Settings

Source: https://docs.filone.com/app/settings

**Settings** is in the user menu at the bottom of the left sidebar. It holds your profile, the organizations you belong to, your notification preferences, and your account security. Every member of an organization has their own Settings.

## Profile

The **Profile** card holds your **Avatar**, **Name**, and **Email**.

- **Avatar**: upload a picture. It saves as soon as it uploads.
- **Name**: up to 200 characters, and can't be empty. It saves on its own when you click out of the field. There is no save button.
- **Email**: click the field to open **Change email**, enter the **New email**, and click **Update**. Disposable addresses are rejected.

Warning: Changing your email address sends you back through verification
Updating the address marks the account unverified, sends a verification email to the new address, and drops you straight onto the verification screen. Every page redirects there until you confirm, exactly as for a new account.

You can change the address again while unverified, so a typo is recoverable.

**If you signed in with Google or GitHub, your name and email are managed there.** Avatar, name, and email are read-only for social sign-ins, labelled *Managed by Google* or *Managed by GitHub* with a link straight to that provider's profile page, so you keep one source of truth for them.

Your organization's name is not part of your profile. Owners and Admins rename it on the **Edit organization** page, opened from the organization menu at the top of the left sidebar, where the name must be 2 to 100 characters, using letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, and periods only.

## Organizations

The **Organizations** section lists every organization you belong to, with your role and when you joined. Each row's menu offers **Switch to this organization** and **Leave organization**. Leaving removes your access to that organization and everything in it, and you can only rejoin with a new invitation. The last Owner of an organization can't leave it. See [Organization](https://docs.filone.com/app/organization#leaving-an-organization).

## Notifications

**Marketing emails** ("Receive updates about new features") is a working toggle. It reflects your current subscription status, is off until you turn it on, and saves as soon as you flip it.

Note: Keep an eye on the trial caps
There is no notification setting for uploads or storage limits. Keep an eye on the usage cards on the [Dashboard](https://docs.filone.com/app/dashboard), which show your storage and egress against the trial caps. This is worth doing during the trial, where reaching a cap changes what the account can do. See [Usage](https://docs.filone.com/billing/usage).

## Security

Two-factor authentication, passkeys, recovery codes, and password changes all live in Settings under **Security**. Password is managed by your provider on Google and GitHub accounts, so no **Change** button appears.

See [Account Security](https://docs.filone.com/security/account-security) for the full walkthrough.

## Danger zone

The last card on the page is **Danger zone**, with **Delete account**. Deleting your account is not available in the console yet: the card asks you to email [support@filone.com](mailto:support@filone.com), and the team will take it from there.

Deleting an organization is separate, and is covered on the **Edit organization** page. See [Deleting an organization](https://docs.filone.com/app/organization#deleting-an-organization).


---

# App: Support

Source: https://docs.filone.com/app/support

**Support** and **Documentation** are at the bottom of the left sidebar, above your name. **Support** opens the support page.

## The support page

The page is headed **Support**, with "We typically respond within 1 business day" underneath. It has two fields:

| Field | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| **Category** | **Product issue**, **Billing issue**, **General inquiry**, or **Feature request** |
| **Message** | What you need help with |

You don't enter your name, organization, or email: the console sends them with your message from your account. Under the form, "We'll reply to" shows the address the answer goes to. An **Email** field appears only if your account has no email address. Click **Send message**. The form clears and confirms that the team will get back to you within 1 business day.

Note: Where the reply arrives
Your message creates a ticket for the support team, and they reply by email to your account's address. Look for the reply in your inbox, not in the console.

Below the form, **Common questions** answers a few frequent questions, such as whether buckets can be made public. The **More help** panel beside it links to these docs and offers **Report a bug**.

## Other routes

- **Documentation** at the bottom of the left sidebar opens these docs in a new tab.
- The system status indicator links to the Fil One status page, which is the quickest way to check whether an issue is already known. On desktop it sits in the bar along the bottom of the content area; on a phone it is in the sidebar drawer.
- Account deletion is handled over email at [support@filone.com](mailto:support@filone.com), as noted in [Settings](https://docs.filone.com/app/settings).
- For volume pricing, SLAs, or the Business plan, **Contact sales team** in the **Choose your plan** dialog on [Billing](https://docs.filone.com/app/billing) reaches the sales team directly. On the trial or with no plan, **Talk to sales** in the **Need help?** panel beside the billing cards does the same.
